children.text: Chapter 1
atha varṇāśramadharmam
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>dharma</s> (normative duties) of the social classes and stages of life.

children.text: brāhmaṇakṣatriyavaiśyaśūdrāmukhabāhūrupādeṣu jātāś catvāro varṇāḥ
children.translated_text: The four social classes—<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s>—were born respectively from the mouth, arms, thighs, and feet.

children.text: yasmād brāhmaṇo 'sya mukham āsīd iti śrutiḥ
children.translated_text: For the revealed text says, “The <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> was his mouth.”

children.text: pūrveṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ niṣekādyāḥ saṃskārā vidhīyante
children.translated_text: For the first three of these, the rites of consecration beginning with impregnation are prescribed.

children.text: teṣāṃ dvijanmanāṃ vedādhikāraḥ
children.translated_text: Those twice-born men are entitled to study the <s>Veda</s>.

children.text: tasmād brāhmaṇasyādhyayanādhyāpanayajanayājanadānapratigrahāṇi ṣaṭ karmāṇi bhavanti
children.translated_text: Therefore, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has six duties: studying, teaching, sacrificing, officiating at sacrifices, giving, and receiving gifts.

children.text: kṣatriyavaiśyayor yajanādhyayanadānāni
children.translated_text: A <s>Kṣatriya</s> and a <s>Vaiśya</s> have the duties of sacrificing, studying, and giving.

children.text: kṣatriyasya prajāpālyaduṣṭanigrahayuddhāḥ
children.translated_text: A <s>Kṣatriya</s> has the duties of protecting the subjects, restraining the wicked, and fighting.

children.text: vaiśyasya pāśupālyakusīdavāṇijyāni
children.translated_text: A <s>Vaiśya</s> has the occupations of tending livestock, lending at interest, and trade.

children.text: śūdrasya dvijanmanāṃ śuśrūṣā kṛṣiś caiva
children.translated_text: A <s>Śūdra</s> has the duties of serving the twice-born and of agriculture.

children.text: brāhmaṇasyāśramāś catvāraḥ kṣatriyasyādyās trayo vaiśyasya dvāv eva
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> has all four stages of life, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> the first three, and a <s>Vaiśya</s> only two.

children.text: tadāśramiṇaś catvāro brahmacārī gṛhasthovānaprastho bhikṣur iti ||
children.translated_text: The members of those four stages are the Vedic student, the householder, the forest-dweller, and the mendicant.

children.text: upanīto brahmacārī mekhalopavītājinadaṇḍadhārī snātvā tarpaṇaṃ brahmayajñaṃ sāyaṃprātaḥ saṃdhyopāsanasamiddhomau ca kurvan guroḥ pādāv upasaṃgṛhya nityābhivandī vratenādhyayanaṃ karoti sthite gurau stheyād utthite pūrvam utthāya vrajantam anugacched āsīne śayāne ca niyukto nīcair anvāsanaśayane kuryād anukto yat kiṃcit karma nācarati anukto 'pi svādhyāyanityakarmāṇy ācared uṣṇāmbusnānadantadhāvanāñjanānulepanagandhapuṣpopānaṭchatradivāsvāparetaḥskandastrīdarśanasparśanamaithunānikāmakrodhalobhamohamadamātsaryahiṃsādīni varjayitvā sadāśuśrūṣur guroḥ priyahitakarmāṇi kurvīta adveṣī vākcittānukūlaḥ priyaṃ satyaṃ vadaty ārto 'py asatyāpriyaṃ nindaṃ nācakṣīta madhumāṃsamatsyarasaśuktādyabhojyabhojanavarjī bhaikṣācaraṇaṃ kṛtvā guruṇānujñāto bhaikṣānnam aśnīyād guruvṛddhadīkṣitānām ākhyāṃ na brūyād gurvabhāve tatputre ca guruvat karmācarati ||
children.translated_text: After initiation, a Vedic student wears a girdle, sacred thread, antelope skin, and staff. Having bathed, he performs the libation, the <s>Brahmayajña</s>, the evening and morning twilight worship, and the two offerings of kindling. Grasping his teacher’s feet and saluting him every day, he studies under a vow. He should stand when his teacher stands; when the teacher rises, he should rise before him, and he should follow him when he walks. When the teacher is seated or lying down, the student, when directed, should attend him from a lower seat or bed. He undertakes no action whatsoever without being told, though even without being told he should perform private recitation and his obligatory rites. He must abstain from bathing in hot water, cleaning his teeth, applying collyrium or ointment, perfumes, flowers, sandals, an umbrella, sleeping by day, emission of semen, looking at or touching women, sexual intercourse, desire, anger, greed, delusion, pride, jealousy, violence, and the like. Always eager to serve, he should do what is pleasing and beneficial to his teacher, bearing no hatred and being agreeable in speech and thought. He speaks what is pleasant and true; even when distressed, he should not utter false or disagreeable speech or slander. Abstaining from forbidden foods such as honey, meat, fish, broth, and fermented preparations, he should go begging and, with his teacher’s permission, eat the food obtained as alms. He should not pronounce the personal names of his teacher, elders, or consecrated persons. In his teacher’s absence, he performs his duties toward the teacher’s son just as toward the teacher.

children.text: brahmacāriṇaś caturvidhā gāyatro brāhmaḥ prājāpatyo naiṣṭhika iti gāyatropanayanād ūrdhvaṃ trirātram akṣāralavaṇāśī gāyatrīm adhītyā sāvitravratasamāpter atra vratacārī brāhmaḥ sāvitravratād ūrdhvam anabhiśastāpatitānāṃ gṛhasthānāṃ gṛheṣu bhaikṣācaraṇaṃ vedavratacaraṇaṃ ca kṛtvādvādaśa samā viṃśatisamā vā gurukule sthitvā vedān vedau vedaṃ vā sūtrasahitam adhyayanaṃ kṛtvā gārhasthyānusaraṇaṃ kuryāt prājāpatyaḥ snātvā nityakarmabrahmacaryaśīlo nārāyaṇaparāyaṇo vedavedāṅgārthān vicārya dārasaṃgrahaṇaṃ karoti prājāpatye trisaṃvatsarād ūrdhvaṃ na tiṣṭhedity ṛṣayo vadanti naiṣṭhikaḥ kāṣāyaṃ dhātuvastram ajinaṃ valkalaṃ vā paridhāya jaṭī śikhī vā mekhalī daṇḍī sūtrājinadhārī brahmacārī śucir akṣāralavaṇāśī yāvad ātmano viprayogas tāvad gurukule sthitvā niveditabhaikṣabhojī bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Vedic students are of four kinds: the <s>Gāyatra</s>, <s>Brāhma</s>, <s>Prājāpatya</s>, and <s>Naiṣṭhika</s>. After initiation, the <s>Gāyatra</s> eats food without alkali or salt for three nights, learns the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and observes the vow there until completion of the <s>Sāvitra</s> vow. After the <s>Sāvitra</s> vow, the <s>Brāhma</s> goes begging at the homes of householders who are neither censured nor fallen, observes the Vedic vows, and remains in his teacher’s household for twelve or twenty years. After studying three Vedas, two Vedas, or one Veda together with its ritual manual, he should enter the householder’s life. Having taken the concluding bath, the <s>Prājāpatya</s> performs his daily duties, practices chastity, is wholly devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, reflects upon the meanings of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, and takes a wife. The seers say that one should not remain in the <s>Prājāpatya</s> state for more than three years. The <s>Naiṣṭhika</s> wears an ochre-dyed mineral-colored garment, an antelope skin, or bark; wears matted hair or a topknot, a girdle, and a staff; bears the sacred thread and antelope skin; remains pure; and eats food without alkali or salt. Remaining in his teacher’s household until his separation from the self—that is, for life—he eats alms after first presenting them to his teacher.

children.text: dārān saṃgṛhya gṛhastho 'pi snānādiniyamācāro nityam aupāsanaṃ kṛtvā pākayajñayājī vaiśvadevahomānte gṛhāgataṃ guruṃ snātakaṃ ca pratyutthāyābhivandyāsanapādyācamanāni pradāya ghṛtadadhikṣīramiśraṃ madhuparkaṃ ca dattvānnādyair yathāśakti bhojayati bhikṣūn brahmacāriṇo 'tithīn vedavidaḥ śrotriyān pitṛvyācāryartvijmātulaśvaśurādīn abhyāgatān bālavṛddhān anāthārtādhvaśrāntāṃś ca yathārthaṃ pūjayaty aśakto 'pyagraṃ bhikṣāṃ vā sodakaṃ dattvā śeṣaṃ bhuñjīta dayāsatyaśaucācārayutaḥ svādhyāyatarpaṇābhyām ṛṣīn yajñabalihomajalapuṣpādyair devān śrāddhaiḥ putraiś ca pitṝn balinā bhūtān annādyair manuṣyāṃś ca nityam arcayed ṛṇatrayeṇa mukto 'nṛṇo bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Having taken a wife, the householder too follows the prescribed observances beginning with bathing. He regularly performs the domestic fire offering and the cooked-food sacrifices. At the conclusion of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> offering, when a teacher or a graduate student comes to his home, he rises to meet and salute him, provides a seat, water for washing the feet, and water for sipping, gives him the honey mixture blended with ghee, curds, and milk, and feeds him with food and other provisions according to his means. He fittingly honors mendicants, Vedic students, guests, knowers of the Veda, learned <s>Śrotriyas</s>, paternal uncles, teachers, officiating priests, maternal uncles, fathers-in-law and other visitors, children, the elderly, orphans, the afflicted, and travelers wearied by the road. Even if unable to do more, he should give the first portion or alms together with water and then eat what remains. Endowed with compassion, truthfulness, purity, and proper conduct, he should daily honor the seers through private recitation and libations; the gods through sacrifice, offerings, fire oblations, water, flowers, and the like; the ancestors through ancestral rites and sons; living beings through food offerings; and human beings through food and other provisions. Released from the three debts, he becomes free of debt.

children.text: gṛhasthāś caturvidhā vārttāvṛttiḥ śālīnavṛttir yāyāvaro ghorācārikaś ceti vārttāvṛttiḥ kṛṣigorakṣyavāṇijyopajīvī śālīnavṛttir niyamair yutaḥ pākayajñair iṣṭvāgnīn adhāya pakṣe pakṣe darśapūrṇamāsayājī caturṣu caturṣu māseṣu cāturmāsyayājī ṣaṭsu ṣaṭsu māseṣu paśubandhayājī pratisaṃvatsaraṃ somayājī ca yāyāvaro haviryajñaiḥ somayajñaiś ca yajate yājayaty adhīte 'dhyāpayati dadāti pratigṛhṇāti ṣaṭkarmanirato nityamagniparicaraṇam atithibhyo 'bhyāgatebhyo 'nnādyaṃ ca kurute ghorācāriko niyamair yukto yajate na yājayaty adhīte nādhyāpayati dadāti na pratigṛhṇāty uñchavṛttim upajīvati nārāyaṇaparāyaṇaḥ sāyaṃprātar agnihotraṃ hutvā mārgaśīrṣajyeṣṭhamāsayor asidhārāvrataṃ vanauṣadhibhir agniparicaraṇaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: Householders are of four kinds: one who follows the <s>vārttāvṛtti</s> (productive livelihood), one who follows the <s>śālīnavṛtti</s> (settled livelihood), the <s>yāyāvara</s> (wandering practitioner), and the <s>ghorācārika</s> (practitioner of severe discipline). One following the <s>vārttāvṛtti</s> lives by agriculture, cattle keeping, and trade. One following the <s>śālīnavṛtti</s> observes the prescribed restraints; after performing the <s>pākayajñas</s> (domestic offerings) and establishing the sacred fires, he sacrifices at the new- and full-moon rites every fortnight, at the <s>cāturmāsya</s> rites every four months, with an animal offering every six months, and with <s>soma</s> every year. The <s>yāyāvara</s> performs and officiates at <s>haviryajñas</s> and <s>somayajñas</s>, studies and teaches, gives and receives gifts, and remains constantly devoted to these six duties; he tends the fire and provides food and drink for guests and visitors. The <s>ghorācārika</s>, disciplined by restraints, sacrifices but does not officiate for others, studies but does not teach, gives but does not receive, and lives by gleaning. Devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, he offers the <s>agnihotra</s> morning and evening, undertakes the sword-edge vow in the months of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> and <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>, and tends the fire with forest plants.

children.text: gṛhasthaḥ sapatnīkaḥ pañcāgnibhis tretāgnibhirvā gṛhād vanāśramaṃ yāsyann āhitāgnir anāhitāgniś caupāsanam araṇyāmāropya gṛhe mathitvā śrāmaṇakīyavidhānenādhāyāghāraṃ hutvāśrāmaṇakāgnim ādāya tṛtīyam āśramaṃ gacchet pūrvavad agnyālayaprokṣaṇollekhanādikarma kuryāt tṛtīyām api vediṃ parimṛjya ṣaḍaṅgulāgner darbhair grathite 'dhas tridhākṛtaṃ rajjuvat mūle baddhaṃ ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgulapramāṇaṃ paristaraṇakūrcaṃ kṛtvā madhyavedyāṃ paristṛṇāti śrāmaṇakaṃ śrāmaṇakayajñaṃ yajñadaivaviśvān devānityantam āvāhyājyaṃ nirūpya śrāmaṇakāya svāhā śrāmaṇakayajñāya svāhā yajñadaivataviśvebhyo devebhyaḥ svāhety antaṃ hutvā caruṃ juhuyād ity ādhāraviśeṣaḥ śrāmaṇakāgneś cordhvavedir dvātriṃśadaṅgulyāyatā caturaṅgulivistāronnatā madhyamā tatparigatā pañcāṅgulivistārā caturaṅgulotsedhā adhastād ūrdhvavedivistāronnatā tṛtīyā vedir dvādaśāṅgulaṃ madhye nimnaṃ trivedisahitaṃ kuṇḍaṃ kṛtvādhāya vanastho nityam aupāsanavat sāyaṃprātar āhutīr hutvā mahāvyāhṛtibhiḥ śrāmaṇakāgniṃ juhuyāt patnīko dārair agnibhir vinā vanaṃ gacchet ||
children.translated_text: When a householder accompanied by his wife, equipped with the five fires or the three sacred fires, is about to leave his home for the forest stage, then, whether he has previously established the sacred fires or not, he should transfer the domestic fire to the fire sticks. Having kindled it by friction at home, established it according to the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> procedure, and poured the preliminary oblation, he should take up the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire and proceed to the third stage of life. As before, he should perform the sprinkling and marking of the fire enclosure and the other rites. After cleaning the third altar as well, he should make a strewing-brush of <s>darbha</s> grass, thirty-six <s>aṅgulas</s> long, braided for six <s>aṅgulas</s>, divided into three below, and bound at the base like a rope, and spread it over the middle altar. He should invoke, down to the end of the formula, <s>Śrāmaṇaka</s>, the <s>Śrāmaṇaka</s> sacrifice, <s>Yajñadaiva</s>, and all the gods; allot the clarified butter; offer with the formulas, 'Homage to <s>Śrāmaṇaka</s>; homage to the <s>Śrāmaṇaka</s> sacrifice; homage to <s>Yajñadaiva</s> and all the gods'; and then offer the cooked oblation. This is the special form of the preliminary offering. For the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire, the upper altar is thirty-two <s>aṅgulas</s> long and four <s>aṅgulas</s> wide and high. The middle altar surrounding it is five <s>aṅgulas</s> wide and four <s>aṅgulas</s> high. Beneath it is a third altar corresponding in width and height to the upper altar. After making a fire-pit furnished with the three altars and depressed twelve <s>aṅgulas</s> in the middle, he should establish the fire. Dwelling in the forest, he should regularly offer the morning and evening oblations as at the domestic fire and offer into the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire with the great utterances. A man who has a wife should go to the forest without his wife and the fires.

children.text: vānaprasthāḥ sapatnīkāpatnīkāś ceti sapatnīkāś caturvidhā audumbaro vairiñco vālakhilyaḥ phenapaś ceti audumbaro 'kṛṣṭaphalāvāpyauṣadhibhojī mūlaphalāśī vāṇahiṅgulaśunamadhumatsyamāṃsapūtyannadhānyāmlaparasparśanaparapākavarjī devarṣipitṛmanuṣyapūjī vanacaro grāmabahiṣkṛtaḥ sāyaṃprātar agnihotraṃ hutvā śrāmaṇakāgnihomaṃ vaiśvadevahomaṃ kurvaṃs tapaḥ samācarati śrāmaṇakāgnim ekam evādhāya juhotīty eke vairiñcaḥ prātryāṃ diśaṃ prekṣate tāṃ diśaṃ gatvā tatra priyaṅguyavaśyāmākanīvārādibhir labdhaiḥ svakīyān atithīṃś ca poṣayitvāgnihotraśrāmaṇakavaiśvadevahomī nārāyaṇaparāyaṇas tapaḥśīlo bhavati vālakhilyo jaṭādharaś cīravalkalavasano 'rkāgniḥ kārttikyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ puṣkalaṃ bhuktam utsṛjyānyathā śeṣān māsān upajīvya tapaḥ kuryāt asya sūrya evāgnir bhavatīty āmananti phenapa uddaṇḍaka unmattako nirodhakaḥ śīrṇapatitapattrāhārī cāndrāyaṇavrataṃ caran pṛthivīśāyī nārāyaṇaṃ dhyāyan mokṣam eva prārthayate ||
children.translated_text: Forest dwellers are either accompanied by their wives or without wives. Those accompanied by their wives are of four kinds: the <s>Audumbara</s>, <s>Vairiñca</s>, <s>Vālakhilya</s>, and <s>Phenapa</s>. The <s>Audumbara</s> eats uncultivated fruits and sown herbs, or lives on roots and fruits. He avoids salt, asafoetida, garlic, honey, fish, meat, stale food, grain, sour substances, food touched by another, and food cooked by another. He honors gods, seers, ancestors, and human beings, roams the forest, and remains outside the village. Offering the <s>agnihotra</s> morning and evening and performing the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s>-fire and <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> offerings, he practices austerity. Some say that he establishes and offers into only the single <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire. The <s>Vairiñca</s> looks toward a direction in the morning and goes in that direction. There he obtains <s>priyaṅgu</s>, barley, millet, wild rice, and similar foods; after sustaining himself and his guests with them, he performs the <s>agnihotra</s>, <s>śrāmaṇaka</s>, and <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> offerings, remains devoted to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and is given to austerity. The <s>Vālakhilya</s> wears matted hair and garments of rags and bark, and has the sun for his fire. At the full moon of <s>Kārttikī</s>, he gives up abundant food that has been consumed and subsists otherwise through the remaining months while practicing austerity. The authorities declare that the sun alone is his fire. The <s>Phenapa</s>, designated <s>Uddaṇḍaka</s>, <s>Unmattaka</s>, and <s>Nirodhaka</s>, eats withered leaves that have fallen, observes the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> vow, sleeps on the ground, meditates on <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, and seeks liberation alone.

children.text: apatnīkā bahuvidhāḥ kālāśikā uddaṇḍasaṃvṛttā aśmakuṭṭā udagraphalino dantolūkhalikā uñchavṛttikāḥ saṃdarśanavṛttikāḥ kapotavṛttikā mṛgacārikā hastādāyinaḥ śailaphalakādino 'rkadagdhāśino bailvāśinaḥ kusumāśinaḥ pāṇḍupattrāśinaḥ kālāntarabhojina ekakālikāś catuṣkālikāḥ kaṇṭakaśāyino vīrāsanaśāyinaḥ pañcāgnimadhyaśāyino dhūmāśinaḥ pāṣāṇaśāyino 'bhyavagāhina udakumbhavāsino mauninaś cāvākśirasaḥ sūryapratimukhā ūrdhvabāhukā ekapādasthitāś ceti vividhācārā bhavantīti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Those without wives are of many kinds: the <s>Kālāśikas</s>, those who follow the <s>Uddaṇḍa</s> discipline, stone-pounders, eaters of raised fruit, those who use their teeth as a mortar, gleaners, those who live on whatever comes into view, those with a pigeon's mode of life, those who roam like deer, those who receive food directly into the hand, those who eat from stone slabs, eaters of food scorched by the sun, eaters of <s>bilva</s> fruit, flower-eaters, eaters of pale leaves, those who eat only at intervals, those who eat once at the prescribed time, those who eat at four prescribed times, those who lie on thorns, those who sleep in the heroic posture, those who lie amid the five fires, those who subsist on smoke, those who sleep on stone, those who remain immersed in water, those who dwell in water jars, the silent, those who keep their heads lowered, those who face the sun, those who hold their arms raised, and those who stand on one foot. Thus it is understood that they follow diverse practices.

children.text: atha bhikṣukā mokṣārthinaḥ kuṭīcakābahūdakā haṃsāḥ paramahaṃsāś ceti caturvidhā bhavanti tatra kuṭīcakā gautamabhāradvājayājñavalkyahārītaprabhṛtīnām āśrameṣv aṣṭau grāsāṃś caranto yogamārgatattvajñā mokṣam eva prārthayante bahūdakās tridaṇḍakamaṇḍalukāṣāyadhātuvastragrahaṇaveṣadhāriṇo brahmarṣigṛheṣu cānyeṣu sādhuvṛtteṣu māṃsalavaṇaparyuṣitānnaṃ varjayantaḥ saptāgāreṣu bhaikṣaṃ kṛtvā mokṣam eva prārthayante haṃsā nāma grāme caikarātraṃ nagare pañcarātraṃ vasantas tadupari na vasanto gomūtragomayāhāriṇo vā māsopavāsino vā nityacāndrāyaṇavratino nityam utthānam eva prārthayante paramahaṃsā nāma vṛkṣaikamūle śūnyāgāre śmaśāne āvāsinaḥ sāmbarā digambarā vā na teṣāṃ dharmādharmau satyānṛte śuddhyaśuddhyādi dvaitaṃ sarvasamāḥ sarvātmanaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcanāḥ sarvavarṇeṣu bhaikṣācaraṇaṃ kurvanti brāhmaṇānāṃ cāturāśramyaṃ kṣatriyāṇāṃ trayāśramyaṃ vaiśyānāṃ dvyāśramyaṃ vihitaṃ tatphalaṃ hi sakāmaṃ niṣkāmaṃ ceti dvividhaṃ bhavati sakāmaṃ nāmeha saṃsāre 'bhivṛddhiṃ jñātvā putralābhādyabhikāṅkṣaṇam anyat svargādiphalakāṅkṣaṇaṃ vā niṣkāmaṃ nāma kiṃcid anabhikāṅkṣya yathāvihitānuṣṭhānam iti tatra niṣkāmam dvividhaṃ bhavati pravṛttir nivṛttiś ceti pravṛttir nāma saṃsāram anādṛtya sāṃkhyajñānaṃ samāśritya prāṇāyāmāsanapratyāhāradhāraṇāyukto vāyujayaṃ kṛtvāṇimādyaiśvaryaprāpaṇaṃ tat punar api tapaḥkṣayāj janmaprāpakatvād vyādhibāhulyāc ca nādriyante paramarṣayo nivṛttir nāma lokānām anityatvaṃ jñātvā paramātmano 'nyan na kiṃcid astīti saṃsāram anādṛtya chittvā bhāryāmayaṃ pāśaṃ jitendriyo bhūtvā śarīraṃ vihāya kṣetrajñaparamātmanor yogaṃ kṛtvātīndriyaṃ sarvajagadbījam aśeṣaviśeṣaṃ nityānandam amṛtarasapānavat sarvadā tṛptikaraṃ paraṃ jyotiḥpraveśakam iti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Now mendicants seeking liberation are of four kinds: <s>kuṭīcakas</s>, <s>bahūdakas</s>, <s>haṃsas</s>, and <s>paramahaṃsas</s>. Of these, the <s>kuṭīcakas</s>, living in the hermitages of <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Bhāradvāja</s>, <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, <s>Hārīta</s>, and others, go about for eight mouthfuls; knowing the truth of the path of yoga, they seek liberation alone. The <s>bahūdakas</s> wear the garb and insignia of a triple staff, water pot, and ochre, mineral-dyed robe. In the homes of brahmin seers and of other virtuous people, they avoid meat, salt, and stale food; after begging from seven houses, they seek liberation alone. Those called <s>haṃsas</s> remain one night in a village and five nights in a town, but do not remain beyond that. They subsist on cow urine and cow dung, or fast for a month, or continually observe the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> vow; they always seek spiritual elevation alone. Those called <s>paramahaṃsas</s> dwell at the foot of a single tree, in an empty house, or in a cremation ground, either clothed or sky-clad. For them there is no duality such as <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, truth and falsehood, purity and impurity. They are equal toward all, identify the Self with all, and regard a clod and gold alike; they make their begging rounds among all social classes. Four stages of life are prescribed for brahmins, three for kṣatriyas, and two for vaiśyas. Their fruit is of two kinds: pursued with desire and pursued without desire. Practice with desire means recognizing advancement here in the cycle of rebirth and aspiring to obtain a son and the like, or else aspiring to a result such as heaven. Practice without desire means carrying out what is prescribed without aspiring to anything. In this regard, desireless practice is of two kinds: engagement and withdrawal. Engagement means disregarding the cycle of rebirth, resorting to <s>Sāṃkhya</s> knowledge, becoming equipped with breath control, posture, withdrawal of the senses, and concentration, mastering the vital wind, and attaining powers such as minuteness. Yet the supreme seers do not esteem this, because it leads to rebirth once the accumulated austerity is exhausted and because it brings many illnesses. Withdrawal means recognizing that the worlds are impermanent and that nothing exists apart from the supreme Self, disregarding the cycle of rebirth, cutting the noose made of a wife, gaining mastery over the senses, abandoning the body, and effecting the union of the individual knower of the field with the supreme Self. It is understood to bring entry into the supreme light, which is beyond the senses, the seed of the entire universe, free of every distinction, eternal bliss, and always satisfying like a draught of the nectar of immortality.

children.text: nivṛttyācārabhedāddhi yoginas trividhā bhavanti sāraṅgā ekārthyā visaragāś ceti anirodhakā nirodhakā mārgagā vimārgagāś ceti caturvidhāḥ sāraṅgā dūragā adūragā bhrūmadhyagā asambhaktāḥ sambhaktāś cety ekārthyāḥ pañcadhā bhavanti na saṅkhyāvanto visaragās tatra sāraṅgāḥ sāraṃ kṣetrajñas taṃ gacchantīti sāraṅgās teṣv anirodhakā ahaṃ viṣṇur iti dhyātvā ye caranti teṣāṃ prāṇāyāmādayo na santi ye tu nirodhakās teṣāṃ prāṇāyāmapratyāhāradhāraṇādayaḥ ṣoḍaśa kalāḥ santi ye mārgagās teṣāṃ ṣaḍ eva prāṇāyāmādayo ye vimārgās teṣāṃ yamaniyamāsanaprāṇāyāmapratyāhāradhāraṇādhyānasamādhayaś cety aṣṭāṅgān kalpayanto dhyeyam apy anyathā kurvanti ||
children.translated_text: Because of differences in the conduct of withdrawal, yogins are of three kinds: <s>sāraṅgas</s>, <s>ekārthyas</s>, and <s>visaragas</s>. The <s>sāraṅgas</s> are of four kinds: non-restrainers, restrainers, those who follow the path, and those who follow a wrong path. The <s>ekārthyas</s> are of five kinds: those who go far, those who do not go far, those who go to the space between the eyebrows, the unassociated, and the associated. The <s>visaragas</s> are innumerable. Here the essence is the individual knower of the field; because the <s>sāraṅgas</s> go to that essence, they are called <s>sāraṅgas</s>. Among them, the non-restrainers are those who wander while meditating, ‘I am <s>Viṣṇu</s>’; they have no disciplines such as breath control. The restrainers have sixteen constituent disciplines, including breath control, withdrawal of the senses, and concentration. Those who follow the path have only six, beginning with breath control. Those who follow a wrong path construct the eight limbs—restraint, observance, posture, breath control, withdrawal of the senses, concentration, meditation, and absorption—but also conceive the object of meditation incorrectly.

children.text: athaikārṣyā eka evarṣir yeṣāṃ te ekārṣyās teṣu ye dūragās teṣām ayaṃ mārgaḥ piṅgalayā nāḍikayādityamaṇḍalam anupraviśya tatrasthena puruṣeṇa saṃyujya tataś candramaṇḍalaṃ tatrasthena puruṣeṇa tato vidyutaṃ tatrasthena puruṣeṇa punaḥ krameṇa vaikuṇṭhasāyujyaṃ yanti ye 'dūragās teṣām ayaṃ dharmaḥ kṣetrajñaparamātmanor yogaṃ kṣetrajñadvāreṇa kārayitvā tatraiva samastavināśaṃ dhyātvākāśavat sattāmātro 'ham iti dhyāyanti bhrūmadhyagāḥ kṣetrajñaparamātmanor yoge sattvarūpāgnidvāreṇa bhrūmadhyaṃ nītvā pañcabhyo 'ṅguṣṭhādibhyaḥ sthānebhya ākarṣaṇaṃ punaḥ piṅgalādvāreṇa niṣkramaṇaṃ pralayāntaṃ kṣetrajñayogāntaṃ vā kurvanti asambhaktā nāma manasā dhyānaṃ kurvanti tatpratipādanāgamaṃ śrotreṇa śṛṇvanti cakṣuṣā devatākāraṃ paśyanti ghrāṇena gandham anubhavanti pāṇinā devatāṃ namaskurvanti sambhaktā nāma brāhmaṇaḥ sarvavyāpakatvādyuktam ayuktaṃ yo 'sau paramātmā tat sa vyāpyākāśavat tiṣṭhati tasmād brahmaṇo 'nyan na kutracid ātmānaṃ pratipadyate 'sau bhrūmadhyagatasyāpi saṃśayān niṣpramāṇam evety uktaṃ tasmād brahmavyatiriktam anyan nopapadyate vividhasaraṇād vividhadarśanāt kupathagāmitvād visaragāḥ purā prajāpatir upadeśagūhanārthaṃ visaragapakṣaṃ dṛṣṭavān taṃ dṛṣṭvā munayo 'pi mohaṃ jagmuḥ kiṃ punar manuṣyāḥ visaragapaśūnām ahaṃkārayuktānāṃ janmāntareṣu muktir nāsmiñ janmani tasmād visaragapakṣo nānuṣṭheyaḥ kecid visargāḥ kāyakleśāt kecin mantrajapāt kecid yena kenacid dhyānena kecid yena kenacid akṣareṇa kecid vāyujayād anye paramātmanā kṣetrajñaṃ saṃyojya dhyāyanty ete paramātmasaṃyogam eva necchanti hṛdistha eva puruṣa iti vadanti kecin na kiṃcid dhyānam iti yathoktānuṣṭhānaṃ yogam iti jñātvā muktim icchanti teṣāṃ visaragapaśūnām antareṣu muktir nāsmiñ janmani tasminn eva janmani mokṣakāṅkṣiṇā visaragapakṣo nānuṣṭheyaḥ saguṇe brahmaṇi buddhiṃ niveśya paścān nirguṇaṃ brahmāśritya yatnaṃ kuryād iti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>Ekārṣyas</s>: those who have only one seer are <s>Ekārṣyas</s>. Among them, this is the path of those who travel far. Through the <s>piṅgalā nāḍī</s> (the right subtle channel), they enter the orb of the sun and unite with the <s>puruṣa</s> dwelling there; from there they proceed to the orb of the moon and unite with the <s>puruṣa</s> dwelling there; then they proceed to lightning and unite with the <s>puruṣa</s> dwelling there; and thereafter, stage by stage, they attain union with <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>. This is the discipline of those who do not travel far. Having brought about the union of the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (the individual knower) and the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) through the gateway of the <s>kṣetrajña</s>, they meditate there upon the dissolution of everything and contemplate, “I am mere being, like space.” Those who proceed through the midpoint between the brows, when uniting the <s>kṣetrajña</s> and the <s>Paramātman</s>, conduct it to the midpoint between the brows through the gateway of the fire whose nature is <s>sattva</s>; they draw it up from the five locations beginning with the big toes and then make it depart through the <s>piṅgalā</s>, either until the final dissolution or until the union with the <s>kṣetrajña</s> is complete. Those called the “unjoined” meditate with the mind, hear with the ear the revealed teaching that expounds it, see the form of the deity with the eye, experience its fragrance with the nose, and salute the deity with the hand. Those called the “joined” are as follows. The <s>brāhmaṇa</s> recognizes that the <s>Paramātman</s>, who is described as all-pervading and so forth, abides like space after pervading everything. Because of that <s>Brahman</s>, he does not apprehend any self anywhere as distinct. It has therefore been said that even the claim that it has entered the midpoint between the brows is, on account of its doubtful character, entirely without valid proof. Consequently, nothing separate from <s>Brahman</s> can be established. Because they wander in different directions, hold different views, and follow bad paths, they are called <s>Visaragas</s> (those who disperse). Formerly <s>Prajāpati</s>, in order to conceal the true instruction, adopted the doctrine of the <s>Visaragas</s>. Seeing it, even the sages fell into delusion—how much more ordinary human beings! For the <s>Visaraga</s> beasts, who are bound by egoism, liberation occurs only in subsequent births, not in this birth. Therefore, the doctrine of the <s>Visaragas</s> must not be practiced. Some <s>Visaragas</s> rely upon bodily torment, some upon repetition of mantras, some upon just any meditation, some upon just any syllable, and some upon mastery of the breath; others unite the <s>kṣetrajña</s> with the <s>Paramātman</s> and meditate. These do not seek union with the <s>Paramātman</s> itself, but say that the <s>puruṣa</s> is located only in the heart. Some say that there should be no meditation at all. Understanding the prescribed observance to be yoga, they desire liberation. For those <s>Visaraga</s> beasts liberation occurs only between successive births, not in this birth. One who desires liberation in this very birth must not practice the doctrine of the <s>Visaragas</s>. It is understood that one should first fix the intellect upon qualified <s>Brahman</s> and then exert oneself by taking refuge in unqualified <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: Chapter 2

atha vanasthasya śrāmaṇakavidhānaṃ gṛhasthaḥ somayājī putraṃ pautraṃ ca dṛṣṭvā tatputrādīn gṛhe saṃsthāpya mauṇḍyaṃ kṛtvā prājāpatyaṃ kṛcchraṃ cared vasante śuklapakṣe puṇyakṣetre patnyā sārdhaṃ vanāśramaṃ yāti pūrvasmin divase kṛtasnānaḥ saṃkalpya kuśodakaṃ pītvopavāsaṃ kuryād aupāsanahomaṃ hutvāgnimayaṃ te yonir ityaraṇyām āropayed darśapūrṇamāsavidhānena darbhādīn saṃgṛhya pūrvavat paristaraṇakūrcān paridhīn samidho veṇudaṇḍopavītakamaṇḍaluvalkalādīn saṃbharati pūrvoktavidhināgnikuṇḍaṃ kuryād aparasmin divase vaiśvānarasūktenāgniṃ mathitvā prajvālyāgna āyāhy upāvarohety agniṃ nidhāya pūrvavac chrāmaṇakāgnyāghāraṃ juhoti praṇamyāgniṃ pariṣicyāgne prāyaścitte tvam iti pañcaprāyaścittaṃ hutvāpo hiraṇyāvamānair ātmānaṃ prokṣya brahmadaivatyaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ pañcavāruṇaṃ ca pradhānān vyāhṛtyantaṃ yajet ||
children.translated_text: Now follows the ascetic ordinance for a forest-dweller. A householder who has performed the Soma sacrifice, after seeing a son and a grandson, installs that son and the other members of his family in the household, has his head shaved, and performs the <s>Prājāpatya Kṛcchra</s> penance. In spring, during the bright fortnight and at a sacred place, he goes with his wife into the forest stage of life. On the preceding day, after bathing, he makes his resolve, drinks water containing <s>kuśa</s> grass, and fasts. Having made the offering in the domestic fire, he places the fire in the fire-sticks with the formula, “Your womb is made of fire.” Following the procedure for the new- and full-moon sacrifices, he gathers <s>darbha</s> grass and the other materials. As before, he prepares the strewing grass, grass bundles, enclosing sticks, fuel sticks, a bamboo staff, sacred thread, water pot, bark garments, and the other requisites. He makes a fire pit according to the procedure stated earlier. On the following day he churns and kindles the fire with the <s>Vaiśvānara Sūkta</s>, deposits it with the formula, “O <s>Agni</s>, come here; descend,” and, as before, pours the introductory oblation into the ascetic fire. Having bowed to the fire and sprinkled water around it, he offers the five expiatory oblations with the formula beginning, “O <s>Agni</s>, you are expiation.” He sprinkles himself with water while reciting the text called <s>Hiraṇyāvamāna</s>, and performs the principal offerings to <s>Brahman</s>, the offering to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and the five offerings to <s>Varuṇa</s>, ending with the <s>vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances).

children.text: agneḥ pratīcyāṃ dvau kuśau pūrvāgronyasyordhve 'śmānaṃ nidhāya tat savitur vareṇyam iti dakṣiṇapādāṅguṣṭhāgreṇāśmānam adhitiṣṭhet tejovatsava iti valkalam ajinaṃ cīraṃ vā paridhāya pūrvavan mekhalādīṃs trīṇy upavītāny uttarīyaṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ cādadāty ācamya svasti devety agniṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ praṇāmaṃ ca kṛtvāsīta śaṃ no vedīr iti svamūrdhni prokṣya jayān abhyātānān rāṣṭrabhṛto vyāhṛtīś ca hutvājyaśeṣaṃ prāṇāyāmena prāśnīyād yoge yoga iti dvir ācamya śatam in nu śarada itipraṇāmam āgantrā samagan mahīti pradakṣiṇaṃ cādityasya kurvīta rāṣṭrabhṛd asīty ūrdhvāgraṃ kūrcaṃ gṛhṇīyāt oṃ bhūs tat savitur oṃ bhuvo bhargo devasyauṃ suvardhiyo yo na iti paccho vyastām oṃ bhūr bhuvas tat savitur oṃ suvardhiyo yo na ity ardharcām oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ suvas tat savitur iti samastāṃ ca sāvitrīṃ japtvā vanāśramaṃ praviśya brahmacaryavrataṃ saṃkalpayet ||
children.translated_text: To the west of the fire he lays down two blades of <s>kuśa</s> grass with their tips pointing east and places a stone upon them. Reciting “That excellent splendor of <s>Savitṛ</s>,” he steps upon the stone with the tip of his right big toe. With the formula “You possess brilliance,” he puts on a bark garment, an antelope skin, or a rag. As before, he receives the girdles and other articles, three sacred threads, an upper garment, and a black-antelope skin. He sips water, circumambulates the fire with the formula “Well-being, O gods,” bows, and sits down. Reciting “May our altars be auspicious,” he sprinkles his own head. He offers the <s>Jaya</s>, <s>Abhyātāna</s>, and <s>Rāṣṭrabhṛt</s> oblations and the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, and consumes the remaining ghee while controlling his breath. Reciting “In yoga, in yoga,” he sips water twice. He makes obeisance with the verse beginning “Indeed, may we live for a hundred autumns,” and circumambulates the sun with the formula beginning “The visitor has come; he has assembled here on the earth.” With the formula “You are the sustainer of the realm,” he takes up a grass bundle with its tips pointing upward. He recites the <s>Sāvitrī</s> by its individual quarters—“<s>Oṃ bhūḥ, tat savitur</s>; <s>oṃ bhuvaḥ, bhargo devasya</s>; <s>oṃ suvaḥ, dhiyo yo naḥ</s>”—then by half-verses—“<s>Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ, tat savitur</s>; <s>oṃ suvaḥ, dhiyo yo naḥ</s>”—and finally as a whole—“<s>Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ, tat savitur</s>.” He then enters the forest stage of life and undertakes the vow of celibacy.

children.text: tatpatnī ca tathā brahmacāriṇī syāt svayam evāgniṃ pradakṣiṇīkṛtyājyena prājāpatyaṃ dhātādīn mindāhutī vicchinnam aindraṃ vaiśvadevaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ bāhyaṃ viṣṇor nukādīn prājāpatyasūktaṃ tadvratabandhaṃ ca punaḥ pradhānān hutvāprājāpatyavrataṃ badhnāti sthitvā devasya tvā yo me daṇḍa iti dvābhyāṃ pañcasaptanavānyatamaiḥ parvabhir yuktaṃ keśāntāyataṃ vāpy avakraṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ dvidaṇḍam ādadāti
children.translated_text: His wife too should likewise remain celibate. Having himself circumambulated the fire clockwise, he offers with clarified butter the <s>Prājāpatya</s> offering, the offerings beginning with that to <s>Dhātṛ</s>, the <s>mindāhutis</s>, the <s>vicchinna</s>, <s>Aindra</s>, <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>, and <s>bāhya</s> offerings, the hymns beginning “<s>Viṣṇor nu kam</s>,” the <s>Prājāpatya</s> hymn, and the rite for binding that vow. After again offering the principal oblations, he binds himself to the <s>Prājāpatya</s> vow. Standing and reciting the two formulas “Of the god, you...” and “The staff which is mine...,” he takes up a straight double staff of wood sacred to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, reaching to the hairline and furnished with either five, seven, or nine joints.

children.text: yena devā iti kamaṇḍalumṛdgrahiṇyau pūrvavad upānaṭchatre ca gṛhṇāty agnīn gārhapatyādīn copajvālyāgnihotraṃ hutvāhavanīye prājāpatyaṃ viṣṇusūktaṃ ca sarvatrāgnaye svāhā somāya viṣṇave svāheti hutvāgnīn araṇyām āropayati vane 'drau vivikte nadītīre vanāśramaṃ prakﾱpya yathoktam agnikuṇḍāni kuryāt patnyā sahāgnīn ādāya pātrādisambhārayukto vanāśramaṃ samāśrayaty agnyāyatane prokṣya khanitvā lekhāḥ ṣaḍ ullikhya suvarṇaśakalaṃ vrīhīṃś ca nidhāya śrāmaṇakāgniṃ nidadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: With the formula “By which the gods...” he takes a water pot and a vessel for gathering clay, and, as before, also sandals and an umbrella. Having kindled the fires beginning with the <s>Gārhapatya</s>, offered the <s>agnihotra</s>, and offered in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> the <s>Prājāpatya</s> offering and the hymn to <s>Viṣṇu</s>—in every case offering with “Homage to <s>Agni</s>; homage to <s>Soma</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>”—he transfers the fires to the fire sticks. He should prepare a forest hermitage in a forest, on a mountain, in a secluded place, or on a riverbank, and construct the fire-pits as prescribed. Taking the fires together with his wife and equipped with vessels and the other requisites, he enters the forest hermitage. At the site of the fire he should sprinkle the ground, dig it, draw six lines, deposit a piece of gold and grains of rice, and establish the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire.

children.text: vanyān eva pārthivān vānaspatyān kulīrodghātāñchaṇān purāṇān kuśadarbhān ūrṇāstukāṃ plakṣāgraṃ sugandhitejanaṃ gugguluṃ hiraṇyaśakalān sūryakāntaṃ ca saṃbharati vānaprasthān ṛtvijo vṛtvāgniṃ mathitvā gārhapatyādīṃs tretāgnīn pañcāgnīn vāgnyādheyakrameṇādhāyāhutī dve dve hutvā nityaṃ dvikālaṃ vanyair eva juhoti vanāśramī muniḥ snānaśaucasvādhyāyatapodānejyāpavāsopasthanigrahavratamaunānīti niyamān daśaitān satyānṛśaṃsyārjavakṣamādamaprītiprasādamārdavāhiṃsāmādhuryāṇīti yamān daśāmūṃś ca samācarati bhaktyā viṣṇuṃ dhyāyann agnihotraśrāmaṇakāgnihomau dvikālaṃ notsṛjan grāmyāśanaṃ tyaktvā vanyauṣadhīḥ phalaṃ mūlaṃ śākaṃ vā nityāśanaṃ saṃkalpya tirodhā bhūr ityāhṛtyāparāhṇe svayaṃ patnī vā haviṣyam āsrāvitaṃ pacati vaiśvadevānte 'tithīn abhyāgatān prāśayitvā mitaṃ prāśnāti ||
children.translated_text: He gathers only wild substances derived from earth and trees: <s>kulīrodghātas</s>, old <s>śaṇa</s> fibers, <s>kuśa</s> and <s>darbha</s> grass, a tuft of wool, the tip of a <s>plakṣa</s> branch, fragrant kindling, <s>guggulu</s>, pieces of gold, and a sunstone. After appointing forest-dwellers as officiating priests, he kindles fire by friction and, according to the procedure for establishing sacred fires, establishes either the three fires beginning with the <s>Gārhapatya</s> or the five fires. Having offered two oblations in each, the forest-dwelling sage should regularly make offerings twice a day using only forest produce. He observes these ten disciplines: bathing, purity, private recitation, austerity, giving, worship, fasting, restraint of sexuality, vows, and silence; and these ten restraints: truthfulness, non-cruelty, straightforwardness, patience, self-control, affection, serenity, gentleness, nonviolence, and sweetness of manner. Meditating devotedly on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he should never omit the twice-daily <s>agnihotra</s> and the offering in the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire. Having abandoned cultivated food, he resolves that wild herbs, fruit, roots, or greens will be his regular food. After gathering them with the formula “<s>Tirodhā bhūḥ</s>,” in the afternoon he or his wife cooks sacrificial food without draining off its water. At the end of the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> rite, he feeds guests and visitors and then eats a measured amount.

children.text: rātrau nāśnīyād adhastād darbhāṃs tṛṇāni parṇāni vāstīrya suvrataḥ suvratāṃ patnīṃ vinaikaḥ śayīta sāsya śuśrūṣāṃ karoty enāṃ nopagacchet mātṛvan niṣkāmaḥ prekṣetordhvaretā jitendriyo darśapūrṇamāsau cāturmāsyaṃ nakṣatreṣṭim āgrayaṇeṣṭiṃ ca vanyauṣadhībhiḥ pūrvavad yajed anukramān mūlaiḥ phalaiḥ pattraiḥ puṣpair vā tattatkālena pakvaiḥ svayam eva saṃśīrṇaiḥ prāṇaṃ pravartayann uttarottare 'py adhikaṃ tapaḥsaṃyogaṃ phalādiviśiṣṭam ācared atha vāhitāgniḥ sarvān agnīn araṇyām āropya sarvaiḥ saṃvāpamantraiḥ pārthivān vānaspatyāṃś ca sarvān samūhya nirmanthyaitena vidhināgnim agnyādheyavidhānena ca mantraiḥ sarvaiḥ sabhyāgnyāyatane śrāmaṇakāgnim ādhāyāharet sabhyasya bhedaḥ śrāmaṇakāgnir ity āhuḥ apatnīkaś ca bhikṣuvad agnau homaṃ hutvāraṇyādipātrāṇi ca prakṣipya putre bhāryāṃ nidhāya tathāgnīn ātmany āropya valkalopavītādīn bhikṣāpātraṃ ca saṃgṛhyānagnir adāro gatvā vane nivaset tapasāṃ śramaṇam etan mūlaṃ tasmād etadvidhānam enam agniṃ ca śrāmaṇakam ity āha vikhanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: He should not eat at night. Spreading <s>darbha</s> grass, ordinary grass, or leaves beneath himself, the man of good vows should sleep alone, apart from his virtuous wife. She attends upon him, but he should not approach her sexually; free from desire, he should regard her as a mother. Maintaining his semen and mastering his senses, he should sacrifice as before at the new- and full-moon rites, the <s>cāturmāsya</s> rite, the lunar-mansion offering, and the first-fruits offering, using wild plants. Sustaining his life successively on roots, fruits, leaves, or flowers that ripen in their respective seasons and fall by themselves, he should adopt at each successive stage a still greater degree of austerity, distinguished by subsistence on fruit and the like. Alternatively, one who has established the sacred fires may transfer all the fires to the fire sticks, gather all the substances derived from earth and trees with all the commingling formulas, kindle fire by friction, and, by this procedure and the procedure for establishing sacred fires, establish and bring forth the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire at the site of the <s>Sabhya</s> fire, using all the formulas. They say that the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire is a variant of the <s>Sabhya</s> fire. A man without a wife should offer an oblation in the fire like a mendicant, cast the fire sticks and other vessels into it, entrust his wife to his son, and similarly transfer the fires into himself. Taking his bark garment, sacred thread, and other requisites together with a begging bowl, he should go forth without fire and without a wife and live in the forest. This ascetic exertion is the root of austerities; therefore <s>Vikhanas</s> calls both this discipline and this fire <s>śrāmaṇaka</s>.

children.text: saṃnyāsakramaṃ saptatyūrdhvaṃ vṛddho 'napatyo vidhuro vā janmamṛtyujarādīn vicintya yogārthī yadā syāt tad athavā putre bhāryāṃ nikṣipya paramātmanibuddhiṃ niveśya vanāt saṃnyāsaṃ kuryāt muṇḍito vidhinā snātvā grāmād bāhye prājāpatyaṃ caritvā pūrvāhṇe tridaṇḍaṃ śikyaṃ kāṣāyaṃ kamaṇḍalum appavitraṃ mṛdgrahaṇīṃ bhikṣāpātraṃ ca saṃbhṛtya trivṛtaṃ prāśyopavāsaṃ kṛtvā dine 'pare prātaḥ snātvāgnihotraṃ vaiśvadevaṃ ca hutvā vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirvapet gārhapatyāgnāv ājyaṃ saṃskṛtyāhavanīye pūrṇāhutī puruṣasūktaṃ ca hutvāgnaye somāya dhruvāya dhruvakaraṇāya paramātmane nārāyaṇāya svāheti juhoti ||
children.translated_text: The procedure for renunciation is as follows. When a man over seventy is aged, childless, or widowed, and, after reflecting on birth, death, old age, and the other sufferings, becomes intent on <s>yoga</s>, he may then undertake renunciation from the forest stage. Alternatively, after entrusting his wife to his son and fixing his understanding upon the Supreme Self, he may renounce. Having shaved his head, bathed according to rule, and performed the <s>Prājāpatya</s> observance outside the village, during the forenoon he assembles a triple staff, a carrying sling, an ochre robe, a water pot, a water strainer, a clay-gathering vessel, and a begging bowl. Having consumed the <s>trivṛt</s> preparation and fasted, on the following day he bathes in the morning, offers the <s>agnihotra</s> and <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, and prepares for <s>Vaiśvānara</s> an offering baked on twelve potsherds. He consecrates clarified butter in the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire and offers in the <s>Āhavanīya</s> a full oblation and the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, then makes offerings with the formula: “Homage to <s>Agni</s>, to <s>Soma</s>, to the Steadfast One, to the Maker of Steadfastness, to the Supreme Self, and to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.”

children.text: sruci sruveṇa catur gṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā sarvāgniṣv oṃ svāheti juhuyād agnihotrahavaṇīm āhavanīye mṛcchilāmayebhyo 'nyāni pātrāṇi gārhapatye prakṣipati gṛhastho 'nāhitāgnir aupāsane vanasthaś ca śrāmaṇakāgnau homaṃ hutvā pātrāṇi prakṣipet paccho 'rdharcaśo vyastāṃ samastāṃ ca sāvitrīṃ japtvā bhikṣāśramaṃ praviśāmīti taṃ praviśati antar vedyāṃ sthitvā gārhapatyādīn yā te 'gne yajñiyeti pratyekaṃ trir āghrāya bhavataṃ naḥ samanasāv ity ātmany āropayet bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ saṃnyastaṃ mayeti trir upāṃśūccaiś ca praiṣam uktvā dakṣiṇahastena sakṛj jalaṃ pītvācamya tathaivoktvā trir jalāñjaliṃ visṛjen mekhalāṃ catvāry upavītāny ekaṃ vopavītaṃ kṛṣṇājinam uttarīyaṃ ca pūrvavad dadāti ||
children.translated_text: Having taken a fourfold portion into the offering ladle with the dipping spoon, he should offer it in all the fires with “<s>Oṃ svāhā</s>.” He casts the <s>agnihotra</s> offering ladle into the <s>Āhavanīya</s> fire and the vessels other than those made of clay or stone into the <s>Gārhapatya</s> fire. A householder who has not established the sacred fires should cast the vessels into the <s>aupāsana</s> fire after making an offering, and a forest-dweller should do so in the <s>śrāmaṇaka</s> fire. Having recited the <s>Sāvitrī</s> by quarters, by half-verses, separately, and as a whole, he enters the mendicant stage, saying, “I enter the stage of mendicancy.” Standing inside the altar, he draws in the scent of each of the fires beginning with the <s>Gārhapatya</s> three times with the formula “That sacrificial power of yours, O <s>Agni</s>,” and installs them within himself with “May the two be of one mind for us.” After uttering three times in a low voice and three times aloud the declaration “<s>Bhūr, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ</s>—it has been renounced by me,” he drinks water once with his right hand and sips water ritually. Repeating the same words, he releases three handfuls of water. As before, he gives away the girdle, four sacred threads or a single sacred thread, the black-antelope skin, and the upper garment.

children.text: devasya tvā yo me daṇḍaḥ sakhā me gopāyeti tribhis tridaṇḍaṃ yad asya pāre rajasa iti śikyaṃ yena devāḥ pavitreṇety appavitraṃ yena devā jyotiṣa iti kamaṇḍalumṛdgrahaṇyāv ādadīta snātvāghamarṣaṇasūktenāghamarṣaṇaṃ kuryāt ācamya ṣoḍaśa prāṇāyāmān kṛtvā sahasraṃ śataṃ vā sāvitrīṃ japtvā tathā bhikṣāpātram alābu dāravaṃ mṛnmayaṃ vā gṛhṇāti praṇavādyādibhiḥ pṛthak pṛthak saptavyāhṛtibhis tarpayāmīti devebhyo jale 'dbhis tarpayitvādyābhiś catasṛbhiḥ svadheti pitṛbhyas tarpayet ud vayaṃ tamasa ity ādityam upatiṣṭheta jalāñjaliṃ visṛjyābhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo dadyād adhyātmarato yatir bhikṣāśī niyamayamāṃś ca samācaran saṃyatendriyo dhyānayogena paramātmānam īkṣate ||
children.translated_text: With the three formulas beginning “Of the god I take you,” “The staff that is mine,” and “As a friend, protect me,” he should take up the triple staff; with “Beyond this expanse” the carrying sling; with “With the purifier by which the gods” the water strainer; and with “With the light by which the gods” the water pot and the implement for gathering clay. After bathing, he should perform the effacement of sin with the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa Sūkta</s>. Having sipped water ritually and performed sixteen breath controls, he recites the <s>Sāvitrī</s> one thousand or one hundred times. He likewise takes an alms bowl made from a gourd, wood, or clay. With the seven sacred utterances, each beginning with <s>praṇava</s>, he should satisfy the gods with water while saying “I satisfy”; with the first four utterances he should satisfy the ancestors while saying “<s>Svadhā</s>.” He should worship the sun with the verse beginning “Up from the darkness we,” release a handful of water, and grant freedom from fear to all beings. Delighting in the inner Self, the disciplined ascetic lives on alms, practices the restraints and observances, controls his senses, and beholds the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self) through meditative yoga.

children.text: dharmyaṃ sadācāraṃ nivītī dakṣiṇe karṇe yajñopavītaṃ kṛtvotkaṭikām āsīno 'hany udaṅmukho rātrau dakṣiṇāmukhas tṛṇair antarite mūtrapurīṣe visṛjen nadyāṃ goṣṭhe pathi chāyāyāṃ bhasmany apsu kuśe darbhe vā nācaret goviprodakāgnivāyvarkatārendūn na paśyan kuryāt vāmahastena liṅgaṃ saṃgṛhyotthāyodakasya pārśve tathāsīno brahmacārī gṛhastho 'pi śiśne dvir hastayoś ca dvir dvir gude ṣaṭ kṛtvas mṛdaṃ dattvoddhṛtair eva jalaiḥ śaucaṃ kuryāt karaṃ vāmaṃ daśa kṛtvaḥ karāv ubhau ca tathā mṛdādbhiḥ prakṣālayet vanasthasya bhikṣoś caitad dviguṇaṃ bhavati rātrau yathoktārdhaṃ vā retovisarge mūtravac chaucaṃ kartavyaṃ retasas trir ity eke sa upavītī prāṅmukha udaṅmukho vānyatrāsitvā mṛdāmbunā pūrvavat pādau pāṇī ca prakṣālyācamya mantreṇācamati ||
children.translated_text: Now follows righteous proper conduct. Wearing the sacred thread around his neck and placing it over his right ear, he should squat and discharge urine and feces while screened by grass, facing north by day and south at night. He should not relieve himself in a river, a cattle pen, a road, shade, ashes, water, or upon <s>kuśa</s> or <s>darbha</s> grass. He should do so without looking toward cows, a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, water, fire, wind, the sun, stars, or the moon. Holding his penis with his left hand, he rises and goes beside water. Seated there in the same manner, a celibate student—and also a householder—should apply clay twice to the penis, twice to each hand, and six times to the anus, and should purify himself only with water that has been drawn up. He should wash the left hand ten times and then both hands in the same manner with clay and water. For a forest-dweller and a mendicant this is doubled; at night it may be half of what has been prescribed. After an emission of semen, purification should be performed as after urination; some say that clay is to be applied three times for semen. Then, wearing the sacred thread in the usual manner and facing east or north, he should sit elsewhere, wash his feet and hands with clay and water as before, sip water ritually, and then sip it with a mantra.

children.text: brāhmaṇo hṛdgābhiḥ kṣatriyaḥ kaṇṭhagābhir vaiśyas tālugābhir adbhir ācāmeta ātmānaṃ prokṣya pratyarkam apo visṛjyārkaṃ paryety udakasyāgner vāmapārśvaṃ prāṇān āyamya pratyekam oṃkārādisaptavyāhṛtipūrvāṃ gāyatrīm ante saśiraskāṃ trir japet sa prāṇāyāmas trīn ekaṃ vā prāṇāyāmaṃ kṛtvā pūtaḥ śataṃ daśa aṣṭau vā sāvitrīṃ sāyaṃprātaḥ saṃdhyām upāsya naiśikam āhnikaṃ caino 'pamṛjyate dvijātiḥ saṃdhyopāsanahīnaḥ śūdrasamo bhavati brahmacārī svanāma saṃkīrtyābhivādayed ahaṃ bho iti śrotre ca saṃspṛśya guroḥ pādaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ dakṣiṇena pāṇinā vāmaṃ vāmena vyatyasyar āpādam gṛhṇann ānataśīrṣo 'bhivādayaty āyuṣmān bhava saumyety enaṃ śaṃsed anāśīrvādī nābhivandyo mātā pitā gurur vidvāṃsaś ca pratyaham abhivādanīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> should sip water that reaches the heart, a <s>Kṣatriya</s> water that reaches the throat, and a <s>Vaiśya</s> water that reaches the palate. Having sprinkled himself, cast water toward the sun, and circumambulated the sun, he should go to the left side of water or fire and control his breath. He should recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s> three times, preceded by <s>oṃ</s> and each of the seven sacred utterances and furnished at the end with the head-formula. That is one breath control. Having performed three breath controls or one, he is purified. After reciting the <s>Sāvitrī</s> one hundred, ten, or eight times and worshiping the twilight at evening and morning, a twice-born man wipes away the sins of night and day. A twice-born man who neglects twilight worship becomes equal to a <s>Śūdra</s>. A Vedic student should state his own name and salute with the words “I am so-and-so, sir,” and touch his ears. Bowing his head and crossing his hands, he salutes his teacher by grasping the teacher’s right foot with his right hand and the left foot with his left hand. The teacher should bless him, saying, “May you live long, gentle one.” One who gives no blessing is not to be saluted. One’s mother, father, teacher, and learned men are to be saluted every day.

children.text: anye bāndhavā viproṣya pratyāgatyābhivandyāḥ jyeṣṭho bhrātā pitṛvyo mātulaḥ śvaśuraś ca pitṛvat pitṛṣvasā mātṛṣvasā jyeṣṭhabhāryā bhaginī jyeṣṭhā ca mātṛvat pūjitavyāḥ sarveṣāṃ mātā śreyasī guruś ca śreyān parastriyaṃ yuvatim aspṛśan bhūmāv abhivādayed vandyānāṃ vandanād āyurjñānabalārogyaśubhāni bhavanti yajñopavītamekhalājinadaṇḍān pareṇa dhṛtān na dhārayet upākṛtyānālasyaḥ śuciḥ praṇavādyaṃ vedam adhīyāno 'māvāsyāyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ caturdaśyoḥ pratipador aṣṭamyoś ca nādhīyīta nityajape home cānadhyāyo nāsti mārjāranakulamaṇḍūkaśvasarpagardabhavarāhapaśvādiṣv antar āgateṣv ahorātraṃ sūtakapretakayor ā śauce tāvat kālaṃ tisro 'ṣṭakāsu gurau prete ca trirātram anadhyāyaḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: Other relatives are to be saluted upon one’s return after an absence. An elder brother, paternal uncle, maternal uncle, and father-in-law are to be honored like one’s father; a paternal aunt, maternal aunt, elder brother’s wife, and elder sister are to be honored like one’s mother. For everyone, the mother is more excellent, and the teacher is superior. Without touching a young woman who is another man’s wife, one should salute her by bowing to the ground. From saluting those worthy of salutation come longevity, knowledge, strength, health, and good fortune. One should not use a sacred thread, girdle, antelope skin, or staff that has been worn by another. After performing the rite that opens Vedic study, he should diligently and in purity study the <s>Veda</s>, beginning with <s>praṇava</s>. He should not study on the new-moon or full-moon day, on either fourteenth day, first day, or eighth day of a fortnight. There is no suspension of regular private recitation or fire offering. If a cat, mongoose, frog, dog, snake, donkey, boar, domestic animal, or similar creature passes between those engaged in study, study is suspended for a day and a night; in the case of impurity caused by a birth or death, it is suspended for the duration of that impurity. At the three <s>Aṣṭakā</s> observances and when one’s teacher has died, study is suspended for three nights.

children.text: tadbhāryāputrayoḥ svaśiṣyasya coparame manuṣyayajñe śrāddhabhojane caikāham anadhyāyaḥ syāt āpadārtyor aprāyatye vṛkṣaṇau yānaśayaneṣv ārūḍhaḥ prasāritapādo mūtrapurīṣaretovisarge grāme 'ntaḥśave saty abhakṣyānnabhojane chardane śmaśānadeśe saṃdhyāstanite bhūkampe digdāhe 'śanyulkānipāte rudhiropalapāṃsuvarṣe sūryendurāhugrahaṇe ca tat tat kāle nādhīyīta paratreha śreyaskaro vedas tad adhyetavyo 'nte visṛjya praṇavaṃ bravīti laukikāgnau samidhau hutvā bhikṣānnaṃ medhāpradaṃ śuddhaṃ maunī bhuñjīta pauṣe māghe vā māse grāmād bahir jalānte pūrvavad vratavisargahomaṃ hutvā svādhyāyam utsṛjya pakṣe śukle vedaṃ kṛṣṇe vedāṅgaṃ ca yāvad antaṃ samadhītya guror dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā samāvartīṣyāt ||
children.translated_text: There should be a one-day suspension of study upon the death of his wife or son or of one's own pupil, at the rite for human beings, and when eating at a <s>śrāddha</s>. One should not study during the corresponding period in an emergency, in affliction, or in a state of impurity; while mounted in a tree or boat, on a vehicle, or on a bed; while sitting with the feet stretched out; during the discharge of urine, feces, or semen; while a corpse is within the village; after eating forbidden food; while vomiting; in a cremation ground; when it thunders at twilight; during an earthquake, a conflagration on the horizon, the fall of lightning or a meteor, or a rain of blood, stones, or dust; or during an eclipse of the sun or moon by <s>Rāhu</s>. The <s>Veda</s> brings well-being both here and in the next world, and therefore it must be studied. At the end he dismisses the lesson and utters the <s>praṇava</s>. Having offered two fuel sticks in an ordinary fire, he should silently eat pure alms-food that promotes intelligence. In the month of <s>Pauṣa</s> or <s>Māgha</s>, outside the village at the edge of water, he should offer the fire-oblation releasing his vow as before and conclude his private recitation. Having studied the <s>Veda</s> during the bright fortnight and a <s>Vedāṅga</s> during the dark fortnight until he has completed them, he should give his teacher a fee and return home as a graduate.

children.text: madhyāhne śuddhe jale mṛdadbhiḥ pādau hastau ca dhāvayitvācamyāṅgāni saṃśodhyāpaḥ punantv iti jale nimajjed ācānto vaiṣṇavair mantrair viṣṇuṃ hiraṇyaśṛṅgamiti varuṇaṃ ca praṇamyāghamarṣaṇasūktenāghamarṣaṇaṃ kṛtvedam āpaḥ śiveti snāyād āśramiṇaś catvāraḥ snānaṃ nityam evaṃ pūrvoktena vidhinā kāmyaṃ naimittikaṃ ca kurvanti dhautavastreṇācchādya pūrvavad ācamya prokṣyāsīnas tiṣṭhan vā kṛtaprāṇāyāmaḥ sāvitrīṃ japtvādityam upatiṣṭheta dakṣiṇapāṇinā tīrthena brāhmeṇa bhūpatyādīn daivena nārāyaṇādīn kūpyādīṃś cārṣeṇa viśvāmitrādīn paitṛkeṇa pitṛādīn adbhis tarpayitvā brahmayajñaṃ kariṣyann ity amiṣe tvorje tveti yathākāmaṃ yajuḥsaṃhitām ādyāṃs trīn anuvākān svādhyāyaṃ kurvīta naimittikam ṛtaṃ ca satyaṃ cety ādisūktāni catur vedādimantrān vāpy adhīyīta sarvayajñānām ādir brahmayajñaḥ tasmād upanayanaprabhṛty eva dvijaiḥ kartavyo nadyāṃ tīrthe devakhāte sarasi taṭāke vā sāmānye snānaṃ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: At midday, in clean water, he should wash his feet and hands with clods of earth, sip water, cleanse his limbs, and immerse himself in the water while reciting, “May the waters purify.” After sipping water, he should bow to <s>Viṣṇu</s> with Vaiṣṇava mantras and to <s>Varuṇa</s> with the formula “Hiraṇyaśṛṅga”; having performed the expiation of sin with the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa Sūkta</s>, he should bathe while reciting, “These waters are auspicious.” Members of all four stages of life must always bathe daily in this manner, and they perform optional and occasional baths according to the procedure stated above. Having covered himself with a washed garment, sipped water as before, and sprinkled himself, he should sit or stand, regulate his breath, repeat the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, and worship the sun. With water and the appropriate <s>tīrthas</s> of his right hand, he should refresh <s>Bhūpati</s> and the others with the Brāhma <s>tīrtha</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and the others, including <s>Kūpya</s> and his group, with the divine <s>tīrtha</s>, <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and the other seers with the seers' <s>tīrtha</s>, and the ancestors and their group with the ancestral <s>tīrtha</s>. Declaring, “I shall perform the <s>Brahmayajña</s>,” he should perform private recitation of as much as he wishes of the <s>Yajurveda Saṃhitā</s>, beginning with “For vigor, for nourishment,” and its first three <s>anuvākas</s>. On an occasional observance he may also recite the hymns beginning “Order and truth” or the opening mantras of the four <s>Vedas</s>. The <s>Brahmayajña</s> is the beginning of all sacrifices; therefore, twice-born men must perform it from the time of initiation onward. One should take the common bath in a river, a sacred ford, a reservoir made for a deity, a natural lake, or a pond.

children.text: parasyodake mṛtpiṇḍān pañcoddhṛtya snāyāt kūpe tattīre triḥ kumbhenābhiṣiñced ucchiṣṭo nagno vā na snāyāt tathā na śayīta āturo 'psu nāvagāheta āturasya snāne naimittike daśakṛtvo dvādaśakṛtvo vā tam anāturo jale avagāhyācamya spṛśet tataḥ sa pūto bhavati dvikālaṃ homānte pādau prakṣālyācamyāsane prāṅmukhaḥ pratyaṅmukhaḥ vā sthitvā caturaśraupalipte maṇḍale śuddhaṃ pātraṃ nyaset tatrānnaṃ prakṣipya tat pūjayati dvau pādāv ekaṃ vā bhūmau nidhāya prasannartaṃ tvā satyena pariṣiñcāmīti sāyaṃ pariṣiñcati satyaṃ tvartena pariṣiñcāmīti prātar amṛtopastaraṇam asīty ādhāvaṃ pītvā vidhinā prāṇāhutīr hutvānnam anindann aśnāti bhuktvāmṛtāpidhānam asīty apaḥ pītvācamyācāmed ekavāsāḥ śayānas tiṣṭhann asnānajapahomīśuṣkapāda udaṅmukho vā nāśnāti bhinnapātre 'nnaṃ paryuṣitaṃ śayanāsanotsaṅgasthaṃ vā na bhuñjīta añjalināpo na pibed ucchiṣṭāśucyāśaucipatitaiḥ spṛṣṭaṃ sūtakapretake cānnaṃ nāśnīyāt ||
children.translated_text: When bathing in water belonging to another, one should first remove five lumps of earth and then bathe. At a well, one should stand on its bank and pour water over oneself three times with a pot. One should not bathe while polluted by leftovers or while naked, nor should one sleep in that condition. A sick person should not immerse himself in water. For the occasional bathing rite of a sick person, a healthy man should immerse himself in water ten or twelve times, sip water, and touch him; the sick man then becomes pure. At both daily meal times, after the fire-oblation, one should wash the feet, sip water, and sit on a seat facing east or west. On a square, plastered space he should set down a clean vessel, place food in it, and honor it. Setting both feet, or one foot, on the ground, in the evening he sprinkles water around the food with the formula, “O <s>ṛta</s>, I sprinkle you with truth,” and in the morning with “O truth, I sprinkle you with <s>ṛta</s>.” Saying, “You are the covering of immortality,” he should drink the preliminary water, offer the oblations to the vital breaths according to rule, and eat without disparaging the food. After eating, he should drink water with the formula, “You are the lid of immortality,” and then sip water for purification. He must not eat while wearing only one garment, while lying down or standing, without having bathed, recited, and offered the fire-oblation, with dry feet, or while facing north. He should not eat food from a broken vessel, stale food, or food placed on a bed, seat, or lap. He should not drink water from his joined palms. He must not eat food touched by someone polluted by leftovers, impure, under a period of impurity, or fallen, nor food prepared during impurity caused by a birth or death.

children.text: tilasaktudadhilājaṃ ca rātrāv abhakṣyam annaṃ paryuṣitam ājyena dadhnā vā yuktaṃ bhojyaṃ krimikeśakīṭayutaṃ gavāghrātaṃ pakṣijagdhaṃ ca bhasmādbhiḥ prokṣitaṃ śuddhaṃ śvakākādyupahate bahvanne tasmin puruṣāśamanamātraṃ tatraivoddhṛtya vyapohya pavamānaḥ suvarjana iti bhasmajalaiḥ prokṣya darbholkayā sparśayitvā gṛhṇīyāt prasūte 'ntardaśāhe gokṣīraṃ sadaikaśaphoṣṭrastrīṇāṃ payaś ca palāṇḍukavakalaśunagṛñjanaviḍjam anuktaṃ matsyamāṃsaṃ ca varjanīyaṃ yajñaśiṣṭaṃ māṃsaṃ bhakṣaṇīyam udakyāspṛṣṭaṃ śūdrānulomaiḥ spṛṣṭaṃ teṣām annaṃ ca varjayet svadharmānuvartināṃ śūdrānulomānām āmaṃ kṣudhitasya saṃgrāhyaṃ sarveṣāṃ pratilomāntarālavrātyānām āmaṃ pakvaṃ ca kṣudhito 'pi yatnān na gṛhṇīyāt taiḥ spṛṣṭisammiśraṃ parapakvaṃ ca saṃtyajati nityaṃ śrutismṛtyuditaṃ karma kurvan manovākkāyakarmabhiḥ śanair dharmaṃ samācarati ||
children.translated_text: Sesame, parched flour, curds, and popped grain are forbidden foods at night. Stale food may be eaten when combined with ghee or curds. Food containing worms, hair, or insects, food sniffed by a cow, and food pecked by birds becomes pure when sprinkled with ashes and water. When a large quantity of food has been defiled by a dog, crow, or similar creature, one should remove and discard from that very spot an amount sufficient for one man's meal; one may then use the remainder after sprinkling it with ashes and water while reciting “Pavamāna” and “Suvarjana” and touching it with a burning bundle of <s>darbha</s> grass. One must avoid the milk of a cow within ten days after it has calved and, at all times, the milk of one-hoofed animals, camels, and women. Onions, mushrooms, garlic, <s>gṛñjana</s>, things born from excrement, and unspecified fish and meat must be avoided. Meat left over from a sacrifice may be eaten. One should avoid food touched by a menstruating woman or by <s>Śūdras</s> and those born from unions in the regular caste order, as well as their food. When hungry, one may accept uncooked provisions from <s>Śūdras</s> and members of the regular mixed castes who follow their own duties. Even when hungry, one should carefully accept neither uncooked nor cooked food from members of reverse mixed castes, intermediate castes, or <s>vrātyas</s>. One abandons food touched or mixed by them and food cooked by another. Continually performing the acts prescribed by revelation and tradition, one should steadily practice <s>dharma</s> through the actions of mind, speech, and body.

children.text: Chapter 3

gṛhasthāśramī dve yajñopavīte vaiṇavaṃ daṇḍaṃ kamaṇḍaluṃ ca dhārayet snātvā sabhāryo gṛhyāgnau gārhyāṇi karmāṇi śrautāgniṣu śrautāni kuryāt sāyaṃ ca homānte 'tithīn abhyāgatān prāśayitvā mitaṃ prāśya patnyā śayīta ārdrapādaḥ pratyag uttaraśirā na svapity ṛturātriṣu svabhāryām upagacched ādau trirātram ṛtumatīgamanasahāsanaśayanāni varjayet paradārān na saṃgacchet paradāragamanād āyuḥ śrīr brahmavarcasaṃ vinaśyati bhāryayā saha nāśnāty aśnantīṃ tāṃ jṛmbhamāṇāṃ nagnāṃ ca nāvalokayet asatyavādaṃ varjayaty asatyāt paraṃ pāpaṃ satyāt paro dharmaś ca nāsti sarvaprāṇihito 'droheṇaiva jīvec chuddhārthavān kusūladhānyaḥ kumbhīdhānyo 'śvastaniko vā syāt dvijātiḥ patitāntyajātān na spṛśed udaye 'stamaye ca sūryaṃ nekṣeta devaguruvipraghṛtakṣīradadhimṛttoyasamiddarbhāgnivanaspatīn pradakṣiṇaṃ gacchet ||
children.translated_text: A householder should wear two sacred threads and carry a bamboo staff and a water pot. Having bathed, he should, together with his wife, perform the domestic rites in the domestic fire and the solemn rites in the solemn fires. In the evening, at the end of the fire offering, he should feed guests and visitors, eat moderately himself, and lie down with his wife. He should not sleep with wet feet or with his head toward the west or north. He should approach his own wife during the nights of her fertile season. At its beginning he should for three nights avoid intercourse with a menstruating woman, sitting with her, and sleeping with her. He should not associate with another man's wife. Through intercourse with another man's wife, longevity, prosperity, and Vedic eminence are destroyed. He should not eat together with his wife, nor look at her while she is eating, yawning, or naked. He should abstain from false speech: there is no sin greater than falsehood and no <s>dharma</s> (righteous norm) higher than truth. Concerned for the welfare of all living beings, he should live only through noninjury. Possessing honestly acquired wealth, he may keep grain in a granary, keep grain in a jar, or possess no provisions for the next day. A twice-born man should not touch fallen persons or members of the lowest castes. He should not gaze at the sun when it rises or sets. He should pass clockwise around gods, teachers, Brahmins, ghee, milk, curds, clay, water, kindling, <s>darbha</s> grass, fire, and trees.

children.text: snātakarājaguruśreṣṭharogibhārabhṛdantarvatnīnāṃ deyo vātārkaraśmibhiḥ panthānaḥ śudhyanti parasyāsanaśayanāny adattāni nopayuñjīta adatteṣūpayukteṣu svapuṇyacaturthāṃśo jahāti anyopayuktāni vastramālyopānaṭchattrāṇi naiva dhārayed agnau pādaṃ na tāpayed agnāv agniṃ vā devālaye 'gnau jale ca mūtrapurīṣapūyaśoṇitaretaḥśleṣmocchiṣṭāṅganiṣpeṣān na prakṣipet nagnāṃ parastriyaṃ viṇmūtre ca na paśyed ucchiṣṭo devārkacandragraharkṣatārā nekṣeta devagurusnātakadīkṣitarājagośreṣṭhānāṃ chāyāṃ nākramati indradhanuḥ parasmai na darśayen na vadet svapantaṃ nāvabodhayed eko 'dhvānaṃ na gacchet parakṣetre carantīṃ gāṃ dhayantaṃ vatsaṃ ca na vārayej jīrṇamalavāsā na syāt ||
children.translated_text: One should yield the road to a Vedic graduate, a king, a teacher, a superior person, a sick person, a bearer of a burden, and a pregnant woman. Roads are purified by wind and the sun's rays. He should not use another person's seat or bed unless it has been given to him; when he uses such things without permission, he loses a quarter of his own merit. He should never wear clothes, garlands, sandals, or an umbrella that another person has used. He should not warm his feet at a fire or cast fire into a fire. He should not discharge urine, feces, pus, blood, semen, phlegm, leftovers, or bodily refuse in a temple, in fire, or in water. He should not look at another man's naked wife or at feces and urine. While defiled by leftovers, he should not look at the gods, the sun, the moon, planets, constellations, or stars. He should not step upon the shadow of a god, teacher, Vedic graduate, consecrated person, king, cow, or superior person. He should neither point out a rainbow to another person nor speak of it. He should not wake someone who is sleeping. He should not travel a road alone. He should not obstruct a cow grazing in another person's field or a calf that is suckling. He should not wear old, dirty clothing.

children.text: akṣaiḥ krīḍāṃ pretadhūmaṃ bālātāpaṃ ca varjayet keśaromatuṣāṅgārakapālāsthiviṇmūtrapūyaśoṇitaretaḥśleṣmocchiṣṭān nādhitiṣṭhet amedhyalipte 'ṅge yāvat tatlepagandhamanaḥśaṅkā na syāt patitāntyajamūrkhādhārmikavairibhiḥ sārdhaṃ na vased ucchiṣṭo 'śucir vā devagoviprāgnīn na spṛśet devān vedān rājagurumātāpitṝn vidvadbrāhmaṇān nāvamanyeta avamantā nindakaś ca vinaśyati sarvabhūtakutsāṃ tāḍanaṃ ca na kurvīta guruṇā mātāpitṛbhyāṃ tatpitrādyair bhrātṛpitṛbhrātṛmātulācāryartvijādyair vivādaṃ nācaret sarvaśuddhiṣu puruṣasyārthaśuddhiḥ strīśuddhir annaśuddhiś ca śreṣṭhatamā syāt dravyeṣu ratnasauvarṇarajatamayāny adbhiḥ śodhayati tāmratrapusīsāyasādyāny amlavāribhir dārudantajātāni takṣaṇād dhāvanād vā yajñapātrāṇi dakṣiṇapāṇinā mārjanāt kṣālanād vā saṃśodhyāni ||
children.translated_text: He should avoid gambling with dice, the smoke of a funeral pyre, and the heat of the young sun. He should not stand upon hair, body hair, husks, charcoal, potsherds, bones, feces, urine, pus, blood, semen, phlegm, or leftovers. When a limb has been smeared with something impure, it should be cleansed until there is no trace of the smear, no odor, and no doubt in the mind. He should not live together with fallen persons, members of the lowest castes, fools, unrighteous people, or enemies. While defiled by leftovers or otherwise impure, he should not touch gods, cows, Brahmins, or fires. He should not show contempt for the gods, the <s>Vedas</s>, a king, a teacher, his mother or father, or learned Brahmins. One who shows contempt or reviles them perishes. He should not disparage or strike any living being. He should not quarrel with his teacher, his mother and father, their fathers and other elders, his brother, paternal uncle, maternal uncle, instructor, officiating priest, or others of that kind. Among all forms of purity, purity in a man's acquisition of wealth, purity in women, and purity of food are the most excellent. Among substances, he purifies objects made of gems, gold, or silver with water; objects made of copper, tin, lead, iron, and similar metals with acidic water; and objects made of wood or ivory by planing or washing. Sacrificial vessels are to be thoroughly purified by rubbing them with the right hand or by washing.

children.text: carmamayasaṃhatāni vastrāṇi śākamūlaphalāni ca prokṣayed ghṛtādīni dravyāṇy utpūyolkayā darśayet kauśeyāvikāny ūṣair aṃśutaṭṭāni śrīphalaiḥ śaṅkhaśuktigośṛṅgāṇi sarṣapaiḥ savāribhir mṛnmayāni punar dāhena gṛhaṃ mārjanopalepanāpsekair bhūmiṃ khananādanyamṛtpūraṇagovāsakādyair mārjanādyaiś ca śodhayed gotṛptikaraṃ bhūgataṃ toyaṃ doṣavihīnaṃ supūtaṃ vākśastaṃ vārinirṇiktam adṛṣṭaṃ yoṣidāsyaṃ kāruhastaḥ prasāritapaṇyaṃ ca sarvadā śuddhaṃ śakunyucchiṣṭaṃ phalam anindyaṃ maśakamakṣikānilīnaṃ tadvipruṣaś ca na dūṣyāṇi vāyvagnisūryaraśmibhiḥ spṛṣṭaṃ ca medhyam āture bāle pacanālaye ca śaucaṃ na vicāraṇīyaṃ yathāśakti syād viṇmūtrābhyāṃ bahvāpo na dūṣyāḥ parasyācāmatas toyabindubhir bhūmau nipatyodgataiḥ pādaspṛṣṭair ācāmayan nāśuciḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: He should sprinkle articles made of hide, woven garments, vegetables, roots, and fruits. He should strain ghee and similar substances and expose them to a flame. He should purify silk and woolen articles with alkaline substances, cloth made from <s>aṃśu</s> fiber with <s>śrīphala</s> fruits, and conch shells, mother-of-pearl, and cow horn with mustard seeds mixed with water. Earthen objects are purified by firing them again. He should purify a house by sweeping, smearing, and sprinkling it, and the ground by digging, filling it with other earth, having cows stay upon it, sweeping it, and similar means. Water lying upon the ground that is sufficient to satisfy a cow, is free from defects, and is well purified is pure. Something declared pure by word, something rinsed with water and not seen to be contaminated, a woman's mouth, an artisan's hand, and merchandise displayed for sale are always pure. Fruit from which a bird has eaten is not objectionable. Things on which mosquitoes or flies have settled, and their droplets, are not defiled. What has been touched by wind, fire, or the sun's rays is pure. In the case of a sick person, a child, or a kitchen, purity should not be examined too strictly; it should be maintained according to one's ability. Large bodies of water are not polluted by feces or urine. A person sipping water for purification does not become impure from drops of another person's sipping water that fall upon the ground, splash upward, and touch his feet.

children.text: vānaprastho nityasvādhyāyī kuśedhmādīn agnyarthaṃ śākamūlaphalāny aśanārthaṃ ca śucau jātāny āhared anyādhīnam anyotsṛṣṭam aśucau jātaṃ gorasaṃ ca varjayet dhānyadhanasaṃcayaṃ na kurvīta vastraṃ nācchādayet madhūkte toyaṃ māṃsokte paiṣṭikaṃ gṛhṇāti sarvabhūteṣu dayāluḥ samaḥ kṣāntaḥ śucir nirasūyakaḥ sukhe niḥspṛho maṅgalyavāṇīrṣyākārpaṇyavarjī matsyādīn daṃśakān sīrakṛṣṭajātāni kandamūlaphalaśākādīni ca tyajan jaṭāśmaśruromanakhāni dhārayaṃs trikālasnāyī dharā āśayo vanyair eva carupuroḍāśān nirvapet palāṇḍvādīn niryāsaṃ śvetavṛntākaṃ suniṣaṇṇakaṃ śleṣmātakaṃ vrajakaliṃ citrakaṃ śigruṃ bhūstṛṇaṃ kovidāraṃ mūlakaṃ ca varjayati muneḥ sarvaṃ māṃsaṃ gomāṃsatulyaṃ dhānyāmlaṃ surāsamaṃ bhavati pūrvasaṃcitāśanaṃ pūrvāṇi vasanāny āśvayuje māsi tyajati vedavedāntena dhyānayogī tapaḥ samācarati apatnīko 'nagnir adāro 'niketano vṛkṣamūle vasan vanasthāśrameṣu gṛhasthānāṃ gṛheṣu vā bhikṣāṃ bhikṣitvāmbupārśve śuddhe parṇe prāṇayātrāmātram annaṃ bhikṣuvad aśnāti śarīraṃ śoṣayann uttaram uttaraṃ tīvraṃ tapaḥ kuryāt ||
children.translated_text: A forest-dweller, devoted to daily private recitation, should gather <s>kuśa</s> grass, fuel, and the like for the fire, and greens, roots, and fruits for food, all grown in a clean place. He should avoid anything belonging to another, anything discarded by another, anything grown in an impure place, and products of cow's milk. He should not accumulate grain or wealth and should not cover himself with cloth. Where honey is prescribed, he takes water, and where meat is prescribed, a preparation of flour. He should be compassionate and impartial toward all beings, patient, pure, free from fault-finding, indifferent to pleasure, auspicious in speech, and free from envy and meanness. Abandoning fish and other biting creatures, as well as bulbs, roots, fruits, greens, and the like grown on ploughed land, he should maintain matted hair, beard, body hair, and nails, bathe three times daily, and sleep on the ground. He should prepare the <s>caru</s> and <s>puroḍāśa</s> offerings solely from forest produce. He avoids <s>palāṇḍu</s>, other similar plants, plant exudates, <s>śvetavṛntāka</s>, <s>suniṣaṇṇaka</s>, <s>śleṣmātaka</s>, <s>vrajakali</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>śigru</s>, <s>bhūstṛṇa</s>, <s>kovidāra</s>, and <s>mūlaka</s>. For a sage, all meat is equivalent to beef, and sour grain liquor is equivalent to <s>surā</s>. In the month of <s>Āśvayuja</s>, he gives up previously stored food and his old garments. Devoted to the yoga of meditation, he practices austerity through the <s>Veda</s> and <s>Vedānta</s>. Without wife, fire, household ties, or fixed dwelling, he lives at the foot of a tree. After begging alms at forest hermitages or at householders' homes, he eats like a mendicant, on a clean leaf beside water, only as much food as will sustain life. Mortifying his body, he should undertake austerity of ever-increasing severity.

children.text: bhikṣuḥ snātvā nityaṃ praṇavenātmānaṃ tarpayet tenaiva namaskuryāt ṣaḍavarān prāṇāyāmān kṛtvā śatāvarāṃ sāvitrīṃ japtvā saṃdhyām upāsīta appavitreṇotpūtābhir adbhir ācāmet kāṣāyadhāraṇaṃ sarvatyāgaṃ maithunavarjanam astainyādīn apyācaret asahāyo 'nagnir aniketano niḥsaṃśayī sammānāvamānasamo vivādakrodhalobhamohānṛtavarjī grāmād bahir vivikte maṭhe devālaye vṛkṣamūle vā nivaset cāturmāsād anyatraikāhād ūrdhvam ekasmin deśe na vased varṣāḥ śaraccāturmāsyam ekatraiva vaset tridaṇḍe kāṣāyāppavitrādīn yojayitvā kaṇṭhe vāmahastena dhārayan dakṣiṇena bhikṣāpātraṃ gṛhītvaikakāle viprāṇāṃ śuddhānāṃ gṛheṣu vaiśvadevānte bhikṣāṃ caret bhūmau vīkṣya jantūn pariharan pādaṃ nyased adhomukhas tiṣṭhan bhikṣām ālipsate ||
children.translated_text: A mendicant, after bathing, should daily satisfy the Self with the syllable <s>Oṃ</s> and make obeisance with that same syllable. After performing no fewer than six breath controls and reciting the <s>Sāvitrī</s> no fewer than one hundred times, he should perform the twilight worship. He should sip water that has been purified through a water strainer. He should observe the wearing of an ochre robe, total renunciation, abstention from sexual intercourse, non-stealing, and the other restraints. Alone, without fire or fixed dwelling, free from doubt, and equal toward honor and dishonor, he should avoid dispute, anger, greed, delusion, and falsehood. He should dwell outside the village in a secluded monastery, a temple, or at the foot of a tree. Except during the four-month rainy-season retreat, he should not remain in one place for more than one day; during the rains and autumn, the four-month period, he should remain in one place. Having fastened his ochre robe, water strainer, and other requisites to his triple staff, supporting it at his neck with his left hand and holding his alms bowl in his right, he should make his begging round once a day at the homes of pure <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, after the <s>Vaiśvadeva</s> offering. Looking at the ground and avoiding living creatures, he should place each foot down carefully. Standing with his face lowered, he waits to receive alms.

children.text: godohanakālamātraṃ tadardhaṃ vā sthitvā vrajed alābhe 'py avamāne 'pyaviṣādī labdhe sammāne 'py asaṃtoṣī syāt drutaṃ vilambitaṃ vā na gacchet bhikṣākālād anyatra paraveśma na gantavyaṃ bhikṣituṃ krośād ūrdhvaṃ na gacchet bhikṣāṃ caritvā toyapārśve prakṣālitapāṇipāda ācamyod u tyam ityādityāyāto devā iti viṣṇave brahma jajñām iti brahmaṇe ca bhikṣāgraṃ dattvā sarvabhūtebhya iti baliṃ prakṣipet pāṇināgnihotravidhānenātmayajñaṃ saṃkalpya prāṇayātrāmātram aṣṭau grāsān vāśnīyāt kāmaṃ nāśnāti vastrapūtaṃ jalaṃ pītvācamyācāmati nindākrośau na kurvīta bandhūñ jñātīṃs tyajed vaṃśacāritraṃ tapaḥ śrutaṃ na vadet saṅgaṃ tyaktvā niyamayamī priyaṃ satyaṃ vadan sarvabhūtasyāvirodhī samaḥ sadādhyātmarato dhyānayogī nārāyaṇaṃ paraṃ brahma paśyan dhāraṇāṃ dhārayed akṣaraṃ brahmāpnoti nārāyaṇaḥ paraṃ brahmeti śrutiḥ ||
children.translated_text: After standing there only for the time needed to milk a cow, or half that time, he should depart. He should be neither dejected when he receives nothing or is treated with contempt, nor gratified when he receives alms or honor. He should walk neither hurriedly nor slowly. He must not enter another person's house except at the time for alms, and he should not travel beyond one <s>krośa</s> to beg.
