After making his begging round, he should go beside water, wash his hands and feet, and sip water. He should give the first portion of his alms to the Sun with the formula beginning <s>Ud u tyam</s>, to <s>Viṣṇu</s> with <s>Ato devāḥ</s>, and to <s>Brahman</s> with <s>Brahma jajñānam</s>; with the formula <s>Sarvabhūtebhyaḥ</s>, he should cast down a food offering for all beings. Using his hand according to the procedure of the <s>agnihotra</s>, he should conceive his meal as a sacrifice to the Self and eat only enough to sustain life, or eight mouthfuls. If he wishes, he may refrain from eating. After drinking water filtered through cloth, he should perform ritual sipping. He should neither disparage nor abuse anyone. He should abandon relatives and kinsmen and should not proclaim his lineage, conduct, austerity, or learning. Having abandoned attachment, mastered the observances and restraints, and speaking what is pleasant and true, he should oppose no living being, remain impartial, and always delight in contemplation of the Self. Devoted to the yoga of meditation and seeing <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> as the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, he should practice concentration. He attains the imperishable <s>Brahman</s>, for revelation declares: '<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>.'

children.text: saṃnyāsino 'nāhitāgner dehaṃ mṛtaṃ putro 'nyo vā tṛṇair antarīkṛtya śuddhair brāhmaṇair yantreṇa vā saṃnidhāya samudragāmyāṃ nadyāṃ tīre vā saikate deśe sṛgālādibhir aspṛśyaṃ yathā tathāvaṭaṃ khanati gāyatryā snāpayitvā tathā tatrāsayitvā śāyayitvā vā dakṣiṇe haste vaiṣṇavair mantrais tridaṇḍaṃ saṃnyasya savye yad asya pāre rajasa iti śikyam appavitram udare sāvitryā bhikṣāpātraṃ guhyapradeśe bhūmir bhūmim iti kāṣāyaṃ mṛdgrahaṇīṃ kamaṇḍaluṃ ca saṃnyasya pidadhyāt tasmin sṛgālādibhiḥ spṛṣṭe tatkartā pāpīyān bhavati āhitāgner agnīn ātmany āropya saṃnyāsino mṛtaṃ dehaṃ gāyatryā snāpayitvā pūrvavad vāhayitvā śuddhe deśe nidhāya laukikāgnau tadagnim upāvarohety avaropya pavitraṃ ta iti ghṛtakṣīram āsye prakṣipya pūrvavat tridaṇḍādīn vinyasya brahmamedhena pitṛmedhena vāhitāgnimantrais tadagnibhir dahanamācarati tayor āśaucodakabalipiṇḍadānaikoddiṣṭādīn naiva kuryāt nārāyaṇabaliṃ karoti tadvahanaṃ khanitvā pidhānaṃ dahanaṃ nārāyaṇabaliṃ vā yaḥ kuryāt so 'śvamedhaphalaṃ samāpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: For the dead body of a renunciant who had not established the sacred fires, his son or another person should keep it separated by grass, have it conveyed by pure <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> or by means of a conveyance, and dig a pit, as circumstances permit, beside a river that flows to the ocean, on a riverbank, or in a sandy place where jackals and other animals cannot touch it. Having bathed the body with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, he should seat it there or lay it down. With Vaiṣṇava mantras he should place the triple staff in its right hand; in the left, the carrying sling and water strainer with the formula “What of his is beyond the realm of dust”; on the belly, the begging bowl with the <s>Sāvitrī</s>; and at the private parts, the ochre robe, clay-gathering vessel, and water pot with the formula “Earth unto earth.” He should then cover the pit. If the body is touched there by jackals or other animals, the performer becomes guilty of sin. In the case of a renunciant who had maintained the sacred fires, after the fires have been transferred into himself, one should bathe the dead body with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, have it carried as before, and place it in a pure spot. Reciting “Descend into that fire,” he should cause that fire to descend into an ordinary fire; reciting “Your purifier,” he should pour ghee and milk into the mouth; and he should arrange the triple staff and the other implements as before. With the <s>Brahmamedha</s> or <s>Pitṛmedha</s> rite, using the mantras for one who maintained the sacred fires, he should cremate the body with those fires. For either of these renunciants one should perform neither a period of death impurity, offerings of water, food offerings, funeral balls, a single-ancestor rite, nor the other customary rites; one performs the <s>Nārāyaṇabali</s>. Whoever carries such a body, digs and closes its grave, cremates it, or performs the <s>Nārāyaṇabali</s> obtains the fruit of an <s>Aśvamedha</s>.

children.text: nārāyaṇabaliṃ nārāyaṇād eva sarvārthasiddhir iti brahmaṇādyair narair hatasyātmaghātino rajjuśastrodakāśanidaṃṣṭripaśusarpādibhiḥ sarvapāpamṛtasyādāhyānām anyeṣāṃ bhikṣoś caikādaśadinād ūrdhvaṃ mahāpātakināṃ pañcānāṃ dvādaśasaṃvatsarād ūrdhvaṃ sa piṇḍīkaraṇasthāne mṛtakārtham aparapakṣe dvādaśyāṃ śravaṇe vā karoti pūrve 'hani dvādaśa brāhmaṇān nimantrayed apare 'hani viṣṇor ālayapārśve nadītīre gṛhe vāgnyāyatanaṃ kṛtvāghāraṃ juhuyād agniṃ paristīryāgner vāyavyāṃ viṣṭare darbheṣu tadrūpaṃ suvarṇaṃ vā saṃsthāpya puruṣaṃ dhyāyann oṃ bhūḥ puruṣam ity ādyaiḥ prāṅmukhaṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇam āvāhyāsanapādyācamanāni dadyāt puruṣasūktena snāpayitvā nārāyaṇāya vidmaha ity aṣṭākṣaramantreṇa vā vastrottarīyābharaṇapādyācamanapuṣpagandhadhūpadīpākṣatācamanair arcayati ||
children.translated_text: One performs the <s>Nārāyaṇabali</s>, since the fulfillment of every aim comes from <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone, for a person killed by men such as a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, for one who has killed himself, for one killed by a rope, weapon, water, lightning, a fanged beast, an animal, a snake, or the like, for one who has died through any sin, for other persons whose bodies are not to be cremated, and for a mendicant, after the eleventh day. For the five great sinners it is performed after twelve years. In place of the rite of incorporation among the ancestors, he performs it for the deceased during the dark fortnight, on the twelfth lunar day or under the lunar mansion <s>Śravaṇa</s>. On the preceding day he should invite twelve <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>. On the following day he should prepare a fire altar beside a temple of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, on a riverbank, or at home, and pour the preliminary oblation. After strewing grass around the fire, he should place an image of the appropriate form, or a piece of gold, upon a seat of <s>darbha</s> grass to the northwest of the fire. Meditating upon the <s>Puruṣa</s>, he should invoke the east-facing god <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> with the formulas beginning “<s>Oṃ bhūḥ, the Puruṣa</s>,” and offer him a seat, water for washing the feet, and water for sipping. Having bathed him with the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, he should worship him with a lower and upper garment, ornaments, water for washing the feet, water for sipping, flowers, perfume, incense, a lamp, unbroken grains, and further water for sipping, using the formula beginning “We know <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>” or the eight-syllabled mantra.

children.text: keśavādyair dvādaśanāmabhir adbhis tarpayet pariṣicya sahasraśīrṣādyair viṣṇor nukādyair dvādaśanāmabhiś cājyaṃ caruṃ juhuyāt guḍājyaphalayuktaṃ pāyasaṃ havir viṣṇugāyatryā deveśāya nivedya pādyācamanamukhavāsaṃ dadyāt agner dakṣiṇe darbheṣūttarāgreṣu dakṣiṇādy arcayitvā brāhmaṇān pādau prakṣālya navānivastrottarīyābharaṇāni dattvā puṣpādyaiḥ pūjayitvā dvādaśamūrtiṃ dhyāyann upadaṃśaghṛtaguḍadadhiphalayuktaṃ śvetam annaṃ bhojayitvā yathāśakti suvarṇaṃ dakṣiṇāṃ dadāti sahasraśīrṣādyaiḥ stutvā dvādaśanāmabhiḥ praṇamed antahomaṃ juhoty abhīṣṭāṃ parāṃ gatiṃ sa gatvā viṣṇor loke mahīyate ||
children.translated_text: He should satisfy him with water while reciting the twelve names beginning with <s>Keśava</s>. After sprinkling around the offering, he should offer ghee and a cooked oblation with the hymns beginning “The thousand-headed Puruṣa” and “Of <s>Viṣṇu</s> now,” and with the twelve names. With the <s>Viṣṇugāyatrī</s> he should present to the Lord of Gods a sacrificial dish of milk-rice mixed with jaggery, ghee, and fruit, and offer water for washing the feet, water for sipping, and fragrance for the mouth. To the south of the fire, upon <s>darbha</s> grass whose tips point north, he should honor the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> with a sacrificial fee and the other observances, wash their feet, give them new lower and upper garments and ornaments, and worship them with flowers and the other offerings. Meditating upon the twelve forms of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he should feed them white rice accompanied by side dishes, ghee, jaggery, curds, and fruit, and give as much gold as he can as the sacrificial fee. Having praised the deity with the hymns beginning “The thousand-headed Puruṣa,” he should bow with the twelve names and offer the concluding oblation. Having reached the desired supreme destination, the deceased is honored in the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: cāturvarṇyasaṃkareṇotpannānām anulomapratilomāntarālavrātyānām utpattiṃ nāma vṛttiṃ ca ūrdhvajātād adhojātāyāṃ jāto 'nulomo 'dharotpannād ūrdhvajātāyāṃ jātaḥ pratilomas tato 'nulomād anulomyāṃ jāto 'ntarālaḥ pratilomāt pratilomyāṃ jāto vrātyo bhavati brahmaṇo mukhād udbhūtā brāhmaṇā brāhmaṇyaś ca brahmarṣayaḥ patnyo babhūvus teṣāṃ gātrotpannād brāhmaṇyām asagotrāyāṃ vidhinā samantrakaṃ gṛhītāyāṃ jāto brāhmaṇaḥ śuddho bhavet vidhihīnam anyapūrvāyāṃ golako hartṛkāyāṃ kuṇḍaś ca viprau dvau ninditau syātāṃ tasmād adho bāhubhyām āt kṣatriyāt kṣatriyāyāṃ vidhivaj jātaḥ kṣatriyaḥ śuddhas tayor avidhikaṃ gūḍhotpanno 'śuddho bhojākhyo naivābhiṣecyaḥ paṭṭabandho rājñaḥ saināpatyaṃ karoti śuddhābhāve 'paṭṭabandho nṝn pāyāt tadvṛttaṃ rājavat syāt adhastād ūrubhyām ād vaiśyād vaiśyāyāṃ tathā vaiśyaḥ śuddho vidhivarjaṃ maṇikāro 'śuddho maṇimuktādivedhaḥ śaṅkhavalayakārī syāt ||
children.translated_text: Now follows the origin, designation, and occupation of the <s>anulomas</s>, <s>pratilomas</s>, intermediate classes, and <s>vrātyas</s> who arise from the mixing of the four social classes. A person born from a man of a higher class to a woman of a lower class is an <s>anuloma</s>; one born from a man of a lower class to a woman of a higher class is a <s>pratiloma</s>. A person then born from an <s>anuloma</s> man to an <s>anuloma</s> woman belongs to an intermediate class, while one born from a <s>pratiloma</s> man to a <s>pratiloma</s> woman becomes a <s>vrātya</s>. <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> men and women sprang from the mouth of <s>Brahmā</s>; the men became <s>Brahmarṣis</s> and the women their wives. A son born from one of their male descendants to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman of a different lineage, lawfully taken in marriage with the prescribed mantras, is a pure <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. A son born without the prescribed rite to a woman previously belonging to another is a <s>golaka</s>, while one born to a woman taken from another is a <s>kuṇḍa</s>; these are two censured kinds of <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. Below that, from the arms, a son lawfully born from a <s>Kṣatriya</s> man to a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman is a pure <s>Kṣatriya</s>. A child secretly born from those two without the prescribed rite is impure and is called a <s>Bhoja</s>. He must not be consecrated as king; invested with a headband, he serves as the king’s commander. In the absence of a pure <s>Kṣatriya</s>, he may protect the people without royal investiture, and his conduct should be like that of a king. Still lower, from the thighs, a son similarly born from a <s>Vaiśya</s> man to a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman is a pure <s>Vaiśya</s>. One born without the prescribed rite is an impure gem-worker: he should drill gems, pearls, and similar objects and make bracelets from conch shell.

children.text: atha padbhyām utpannāc chūdrāc chūdrāyāṃ nyāyena śūdraḥ śuddho jārān mālavako ninditaḥ śūdro 'śvapālo 'śvatṛṇahārī ca ity ete cāturvarṇikās teṣām eva saṃskāreṇotpannāḥ sarve 'nulomādyāḥ brāhmaṇāt kṣatriyakanyāyāṃ jātaḥ savarṇo 'nulomeṣu mukhyo 'sya vṛttir ātharvaṇaṃ karmāśvahastirathasaṃvāhanam ārohaṇaṃ rājñaḥ saināpatyaṃ cāyurvedakṛtyaṃ gūḍhotpanno 'bhiniṣaktākhyo 'bhiṣiktaś cen nṛpo bhūyād aṣṭāṅgam āyurvedaṃ bhūtatantraṃ vā saṃpaṭhet taduktācāro dayāyuktaḥ satyavādī tadvidhānena sarvaprāṇihitaṃ kuryāt jyotir gaṇanādikādhikavṛttir vā viprād vaiśyāyām ambaṣṭhaḥ kakṣyājīvy āgneyanartako dhvajaviśrāvī śalyacikitsī jārāt kumbhakāraḥ kulālavṛttir nāpito nābher ūrdhvavaptā ca kṣatriyād vaiśyāyāṃ madguḥ śreṣṭhitvaṃ prāpto mahānarmākhyaś ca vaiśyavṛttiḥ kṣātram karma nācarati gūḍhād āśviko 'śvakrayavikrayī syāt ||
children.translated_text: Now, from a <s>Śūdra</s>, who originated from the feet, and a <s>Śūdra</s> woman, a son born according to rule is a pure <s>Śūdra</s>; one born through adultery is a <s>Mālavaka</s>, a despised <s>Śūdra</s>, a horse keeper and gatherer of fodder for horses. These are members of the four classes. All the derivative groups beginning with the <s>anulomas</s> are born from those same classes through their respective unions. A son born to a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> by a <s>Kṣatriya</s> maiden is a <s>Savarṇa</s>, foremost among the <s>anulomas</s>. His occupations are rites of the <s>Atharvaveda</s>, driving horses, elephants, and chariots, riding, serving as the king's general, and the practice of <s>Āyurveda</s>. One born secretly is called an <s>Abhiniṣakta</s>; if consecrated, he may become a king. Alternatively, he should study the eight-branched <s>Āyurveda</s> or the <s>Bhūtatantra</s>, follow the conduct prescribed in it, be compassionate and truthful, and promote the welfare of all living beings according to its rules; or his principal occupation may be astronomy, calculation, and related sciences. From a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> by a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman comes an <s>Ambaṣṭha</s>, who lives by the <s>kakṣyā</s> occupation, dances in connection with fire, acts as a <s>dhvajaviśrāvin</s>, and practices surgery. One born through adultery is a <s>Kumbhakāra</s>, who follows the potter's occupation, and also a barber who shaves above the navel. From a <s>Kṣatriya</s> by a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman comes a <s>Madgu</s>; one who attains the position of guild-master is also called a <s>Mahānarma</s>. He follows a <s>Vaiśya</s>'s occupation and does not perform a <s>Kṣatriya</s>'s work. One born secretly is an <s>Āśvika</s>, who buys and sells horses.

children.text: viprāc chūdrāyāṃ pāraśavo bhadrakālīpūjanacitrakarmāṅgavidyātūryaghoṣaṇamardanavṛttir jārotpanno niṣādo vyāḍādimṛgahiṃsākārī rājanyataḥ śūdrāyām ugraḥ sudaṇḍyadaṇḍanakṛtyo jārāc chūlikaḥ śūlārohaṇādiyātanākṛtyo vaiśyataḥ śūdrāyāṃ cūcukaḥ kramukatāmbūlaśarkarādikrayavikrayī gūḍhāt kaṭakāraḥ kaṭakārī ceti tato 'nulomād anulomāyāṃ jātaś cānulomaḥ pitur mātur vā jātaṃ vṛttiṃ bhajeta kṣatriyād viprakanyāyāṃ mantravaj jātaḥ sūtaḥ pratilomeṣu mukhyo 'yaṃ mantrahīnopanīto dvijadharmahīno 'sya vṛttir dharmānubodhanaṃ rājño 'nnasaṃskāraś ca jāreṇa mantrahīnajo rathakāro dvijatvavihīnaḥ śūdrakṛtyo 'śvānāṃ poṣaṇadamanādiparicaryājīvī vaiśyād brāhmaṇyāṃ māgadhaḥ śūdrair apy abhojyān no 'spṛśyaḥ sarvavandī praśaṃsākīrtanagānapreṣaṇavṛttir gūḍhāc cakrī lavaṇatailavikretā syāt ||
children.translated_text: From a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> by a <s>Śūdra</s> woman comes a <s>Pāraśava</s>. His occupations are worship of <s>Bhadrakālī</s>, painting, physiognomy, proclaiming with musical instruments, and massage. One born through adultery is a <s>Niṣāda</s>, who kills wild animals and other game. From a <s>Kṣatriya</s> by a <s>Śūdra</s> woman comes an <s>Ugra</s>, whose duty is to punish those deserving severe punishment. One born through adultery is a <s>Śūlika</s>, whose duty is to inflict tortures such as impalement. From a <s>Vaiśya</s> by a <s>Śūdra</s> woman comes a <s>Cūcuka</s>, who buys and sells areca nut, betel, sugar, and similar goods. One born secretly is a <s>Kaṭakāra</s>, a maker of bracelets. A child born from an <s>anuloma</s> man by an <s>anuloma</s> woman is likewise an <s>anuloma</s> and should follow the occupation inherited from either his father or his mother. From a <s>Kṣatriya</s> by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> maiden, when begotten with the prescribed formulas, comes a <s>Sūta</s>, foremost among the <s>pratilomas</s>. Initiated without formulas and deprived of the duties of the twice-born, his occupations are instruction concerning <s>dharma</s> and the preparation of the king's food. A <s>Rathakāra</s>, born through adultery and without the formulas, is deprived of twice-born status, performs a <s>Śūdra</s>'s work, and lives by tending, training, and otherwise caring for horses. From a <s>Vaiśya</s> by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman comes a <s>Māgadha</s>. His food is not to be eaten even by <s>Śūdras</s>, though he is not untouchable; he praises everyone and lives by eulogy, recitation of fame, singing, and carrying messages. One born secretly is a <s>Cakrī</s>, who sells salt and oil.

children.text: vaiśyān nṛpāyām āyogavas tantuvāyaḥ paṭakartā vastrakāṃsyopajīvī gūḍhācārāt pulindo 'raṇyavṛttir duṣṭamṛgasattvaghātī śūdrāt kṣatriyāyāṃ pulkasaḥ kṛtakāṃ vārkṣāṃ vā surāṃ hutvā pācako vikrīṇīta coravṛttād velavo janbhananartanagānakṛtyaḥ śūdrād vaiśyāyāṃ vaidehakaḥ śūdrāspṛśyas tair apy abhojyānno vanyavṛttir ajamahiṣagopālas tadrasān vikrayī cauryāc cakriko lavaṇatailapiṇyākajīvī śūdrād brāhmaṇyāṃ caṇḍālaḥ sīsakālāyasābharaṇo vardhrābandhakaṇṭhaḥ kakṣerīyukto yatas tataś caran sarvakarmabahiṣkṛtaḥ pūrvāhṇe grāmādau vīthyām anyatrāpi malāny apakṛṣya bahir apohayati grāmād bahir dūre svajātīyair nivaset madhyāhnāt paraṃ grāme na viśati viśec ced rājñā vadhyo 'nyathā bhrūṇahatyām avāpnoty antarālavratyāś ca cūcukād viprāyāṃ takṣako 'spṛśyo jhallarīhasto dārukāraḥ suvarṇakāro 'yaskāraḥ kāṃsyakāro vā kṣatriyāyāṃ matsyabandhur matsyabandhī vaiśyāyāṃ sāmudraḥ samudrapaṇyajīvī matsyaghātī ca syāt ||
children.translated_text: From a <s>Vaiśya</s> by a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman comes an <s>Āyogava</s>, a weaver and maker of cloth who lives by garments and bronze goods. One born from secret intercourse is a <s>Pulinda</s>, who lives in the forest and kills dangerous wild animals. From a <s>Śūdra</s> by a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman comes a <s>Pulkasa</s>, a brewer who prepares and sells manufactured liquor or liquor derived from trees. One born from a thief's way of life is a <s>Velava</s>, whose work consists of <s>janbhana</s>, dancing, and singing. From a <s>Śūdra</s> by a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman comes a <s>Vaidehaka</s>, untouchable even to <s>Śūdras</s>, who may not eat his food. He lives from the forest, tends goats, buffaloes, and cattle, and sells their fluids. One born through theft is a <s>Cakrika</s>, who lives by salt, oil, and oilcake. From a <s>Śūdra</s> by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman comes a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>. Wearing ornaments of lead and black iron, with a leather strap tied around his neck and furnished with a <s>kakṣerī</s>, he wanders wherever he goes and is excluded from every occupation. During the forenoon he removes filth from the streets of villages and other places and carries it outside. He should live far outside the village with members of his own group. He must not enter the village after midday; if he does, the king must execute him, for otherwise the king incurs the sin of killing an embryo. The intermediate outcastes are as follows. From a <s>Cūcuka</s> by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman comes a <s>Takṣaka</s>, who is untouchable, bears a <s>jhallarī</s> in his hand, and works as a carpenter, goldsmith, ironsmith, or bronzesmith. By a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman comes a <s>Matsyabandhu</s>, who catches fish. By a <s>Vaiśya</s> woman comes a <s>Sāmudra</s>, who lives by goods from the sea and kills fish.

children.text: ambaṣṭhād viprāyāṃ nāvikaḥ samudrapaṇyamatsyajīvī samudralaṅghanāṃ nāvaṃ plāvayati kṣatriyāyām adhonāpito nābher adho romavaptā madgor viprāyāṃ veṇuko veṇuvīṇāvādī kṣatriyāyāṃ karmakaraḥ karmakārī vaidehakād viprāyāṃ carmakāraś carmajīvī nṛpāyāṃ sūcikaḥ sūcīvedhanakṛtyavān āyogavād viprāyāṃ tāmras tāmrajīvī nṛpāyāṃ khanakaḥ khananajīvī khananān nṛpāyām udbandhakaḥ śūdrāspṛśyo vastranirṇejakaḥ pulkasād viprāyāṃ rajako vastrāṇāṃ rajonirṇejakaś caṇḍālād viprāyāṃ śvapacaḥ caṇḍālavac cihnayukto nityanindyaḥ sarvakarmabahiṣkāryo nagaryādau malāpohakaḥ śmaśāne vasan heyapātragrāhī pretam abandhukaṃ visṛjeta vadhyān hatvā tadvastrādigrāhī parādhīnāhāro bhinnapātrabhojī śvamāṃsabhakṣī carmavāravāṇavāṇijyakārī syāt tasmān nikṛṣṭe sute samutpanne patito naṣṭo ghorān narakān vrajati satputro narakebhyas trāyakaḥ pitṝn pāvayitvā tasmād brāhmaṇādyāḥ savarṇāyāṃ vidhivat putram utpādayeyuriti vikhanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: From an <s>Ambaṣṭha</s> by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman comes a <s>Nāvika</s>, who lives by maritime goods and fish and pilots a ship across the sea. By a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman comes an <s>Adhonāpita</s>, a barber who shaves the hair below the navel. From a <s>Madgu</s> by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman comes a <s>Veṇuka</s>, who plays the flute and lute; by a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman comes a <s>Karmakara</s>, a laborer. From a <s>Vaidehaka</s> by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman comes a <s>Carmakāra</s>, who lives by leatherwork; by a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman comes a <s>Sūcika</s>, whose work is piercing with a needle. From an <s>Āyogava</s> by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman comes a <s>Tāmra</s>, who lives by copperwork; by a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman comes a <s>Khanaka</s>, who lives by digging. From a <s>Khanaka</s> by a <s>Kṣatriya</s> woman comes an <s>Udbandhaka</s>, untouchable even to <s>Śūdras</s>, who washes clothes. From a <s>Pulkasa</s> by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman comes a <s>Rajaka</s>, who cleans dust from clothes. From a <s>Caṇḍāla</s> by a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> woman comes a <s>Śvapaca</s>. Marked with the same signs as a <s>Caṇḍāla</s>, he is perpetually despised, excluded from every occupation, and removes filth in towns and other places. Dwelling in the cremation ground, he accepts discarded vessels and disposes of a corpse that has no relatives. He executes those condemned to death and takes their clothes and other possessions. Dependent upon others for food, he eats from broken vessels, consumes dog meat, and trades in hides, armor, and arrows. Therefore, when an inferior son is born, his father falls, is ruined, and goes to terrible hells; a good son rescues him from hell and purifies the ancestors. Thus <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and the other classes should beget a son according to rule upon a woman of their own class, says <s>Vikhanas</s>.
